reports.would_have_quit_at: I would not have quit mid-flow, because the step-by-step prompts kept me moving. I would have lost confidence at step 6 (Ranking), where the app said no papers matched "Grades" and only 1 matched "Sleep", and again at step 8, where the "Known" statement was about telemedicine in Thai ear-nose-throat patients. At that point I would be unsure whether I had done something wrong and would ask my tutor. I would also stop at the final "(mock)" question, since I could not show that to my tutor. I would likely give up on step 7 (quote checking) without help, because the side panel left so little room to read the paper that I only found the quotes by tabbing.
reports.activity:
Signed up as "Mai" (mai.undergrad.qa3@example.com). Created one project, "I'm interested in sleep and grades" (prj_3deda2fcff40427a), and ran all 9 steps to the end.

- Step 2: answered 5 scoping questions, kept the 4 suggested topics and approved them.
- Step 3: ran the PubMed count on the Sleep query, then ran all 8 searches.
- Step 4 to 5: summarised 158 papers. Filtered by study type and article type, opened the Map view and opened one paper.
- Step 6: opened the Sleep ranking and met the "3 topics have fewer than 3 papers" dialog. Chose "Appraise anyway".
- Step 7: rejected 6 "not found, you decide" quotes, which the app said were altered on purpose, and marked the papers as looked at.
- Step 8 to 9: ran the synthesis, got 3 candidate questions and chose Candidate 2: "(mock) Is there an association between sleep and grades among university students?"
- Export: previewed the report. Started the Markdown download and switched the format to the CSV spreadsheet.

No console errors or failed requests appeared at any point. The "Open printable report" link opened a new tab that I could not view with the helper, so I judged the report only from the in-page preview, which showed about 200 of 510 lines. I did not visit My projects, the Settings page or the BibTeX download. I used about 115 helper commands.
reports.categories_and_colours:
Study type has seven categories, each with its own colour and shape: Trial (blue circle), Cohort / case-control (orange-red square), Cross-sectional (teal-green triangle), Qualitative / mixed methods (amber diamond), Systematic / scoping review (pink star), Other design (green cross) and Not reported (grey open ring). The key appears in step 4's mix bars, the 3D map and the step 5/6 chip filters. The same colour and shape are used in the table cells, so I could work out "colour and shape = kind of study" without being told, and clicking a chip filtered the table ("Showing 21 of 158: review article"). Article type (Journal / Review / Preprint / Editorial) is a second row of plain chips with no colour, and filtering by it worked.

What I would query:
- Two overlapping dimensions with no explanation. "Review article" (article type) and "Systematic / scoping review" (study type) look like the same thing to a first-year. The same goes for "Other design" containing "Narrative review" and "Protocol".
- Selecting a chip in each row can give a confusing 0. Trial plus Review article gave "Showing 0 of 158" and the other chips kept their original counts, so I could not tell the combination was impossible.
- Study-type counts change between pages. Step 4 said "Not reported 141 / Trial 5 / Other design 8". Step 5 said "Not reported 20 / Other design 59" and Cohort 4, Cross-sectional 27. A note explains that the AI reads abstracts in step 5, but the first set looked authoritative.
- The green cross (Other design) and the teal-green triangle (Cross-sectional) are close in hue and rely on shape to tell them apart.
- In the Sleep ranking, the filter chips show counts for the 44 papers on screen. That scoping is fine but not stated.
- The 3D map has an unlabeled "height" axis in the retrieval step and a hover-only point identity. The 2D toggle helps, but "Show as 2D chart" is easy to miss.
reports.validity_assessment:
Mostly honest and traceable, but the output cannot be used as a real review in demo mode. Strong points:

- A "Demo mode" banner is on every page and says results will not match my topic.
- AI text is marked "(mock)".
- Search counts and novelty checks are labelled as samples.
- The report opens with "Demo: scripted AI and recorded sample papers; not a real review".
- The ranking step warns that Grades has no matching papers, and the synthesis repeats that.
- Quotes carry a word-for-word check, and tampered quotes are shown with the closest passage and "Accept anyway" / "Reject".
- The novelty text avoids calling anything novel ("Finding no similar study does not prove a question is new").
- The report says it is a scoping aid with a single reviewer and gives search and duplicate counts.

Concerns:
1. The research questions and gaps do not come from the papers. The papers were about telemedicine in Southeast Asia, yet Candidate 2's gap is supported by a quote from "Ilmaskal et al. 2026" (a telemedicine paper). A student could believe the gap was found in the literature.
2. The synonym "sleep means lower grades" came from my own answer and was turned into a search term. This is a keyword-matching error, not a synonym.
3. The one paper selected for Sleep (Thai ENT telemedicine) matched only through "obstructive sleep apnea". The synthesis then listed its age difference under "Known: what the papers agree on", although one paper cannot agree with anything.
4. Search counts are inconsistent. The pre-run count said PubMed 9,245 for Sleep; the run says PubMed 38. The Grades and Measurement queries show identical counts (2,207 / 451).
5. The step 3 "Check the searches" panel did not appear after "Write the searches"; I had to find the Query node myself.
6. The exported question still starts with "(mock)", and candidate 1 dropped "grades".
7. The "(mock)" scripted dialog says each paper has one altered quote, which cannot happen in real mode, so I did not see how real quote failures would behave.

reports.narrative:
I opened Athena as Mai, a nervous first-year who has never written a literature review. The landing page told me within a few seconds what it does and what to click. I signed up, typed "I'm interested in sleep and grades" and was glad the Demo mode banner appeared straight away. At the same time it made me wonder what the point was, if the results would not match my topic.

The scoping questions were friendly, and I liked watching my answers become topics. Step 3 confused me. I clicked "Write the searches" and the panel just showed my topic again with words like MeSH, so I had to hunt for the Query cards to see the actual searches. I also noticed "sleep means lower grades" had become a search term.

Steps 4 and 5 felt reassuring: counts that added up, coloured shapes for study types, and filter chips I could click. The "Trial plus Review article gives 0" moment made me think I had broken something. Step 6 was honest: it told me Grades had no papers and the one Sleep paper was about telemedicine. I appreciated the warning dialog, though I only saw it because I took a screenshot.

Step 7 was the hardest. The panel left very little room, and I found the altered quotes only by tabbing. The explanation that the quote was "changed on purpose" and the closest-passage display made me trust the checking. By step 8 I knew the content was off-topic, so I read it as a demonstration. I chose "Is there an association between sleep and grades among university students?", finished, and downloaded the report. I would not show my tutor a question that starts with "(mock)".

findings.what_happened: The chosen research question and every AI statement in the exported report carry a '(mock)' prefix, and the gap for my question cites 'Ilmaskal et al. 2026', a telemedicine paper, as its supporting evidence. A student could take the report to a tutor believing the gap was found in the literature.
findings.expected: In demo mode, make it unmistakable that the gap and supporting quotes are scripted examples. The exported question should not need manual cleanup, or the export should offer a clearly marked 'sample' watermark only.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the '(mock)' tag, but add a visible 'Demo, not citable' warning beside Download. Where a supporting quote's paper does not match the topic, show 'This paper is not about your topic' next to the quote.

findings.what_happened: Part of my own answer, 'sleep means lower grades', was added as a synonym and used as a search phrase in PubMed and OpenAlex. A first-year would not know that is not a synonym, and the page presents it as part of an approved, defensible search.
findings.expected: Synonyms should be alternative words for the topic (for example 'sleep duration', 'sleep quality'), not my sentence from the scoping chat.
findings.suggested_fix: Filter out synonyms longer than about four words and flag them for review. Add a one-line hint under Synonyms such as 'Other words authors might use for this topic', plus an explanation of MeSH.

findings.what_happened: After clicking 'Write the searches' the panel did not change to show the searches. It stayed on 'Edit this search topic' (a step-2 view), and the PubMed/OpenAlex text only appeared after I switched to List view and clicked a Query row. The step's key content was one click away from where I was.
findings.expected: After 'Write the searches' the panel should open the first query, with 'Check the searches before they run' and the Run all button already on screen.
findings.suggested_fix: Navigate to the first Query node after the searches are written, or add a 'Read the searches' button in the panel.

findings.what_happened: The side panel puts a long checklist, explanation and navigation in front of the paper and leaves about 150px for the paper itself. Page scroll does not move the panel content; I only reached the quotes by pressing Tab. The vocabulary (appraisal, quality checklist, 'AI: Unclear', 'Not reported', 'found word for word') is heavy for a first-year.
findings.expected: The paper's checklist and quotes should be visible without hunting. A short plain explanation of 'appraisal' should come first.
findings.suggested_fix: Collapse the intro and checklist after first view, or open the appraisal in a full-page route like the table. Add 'Appraisal = checking how trustworthy each study is' in one line.

findings.what_happened: 'Known: What the papers agree on' for Sleep showed a single statistic from one telemedicine paper about age and accepting virtual visits. One paper cannot 'agree', and the paper is about ENT patients (it matched only through 'obstructive sleep apnea'). The only 'Sleep' paper was selected through this keyword match.
findings.expected: A single-paper finding should be labelled as such ('1 paper reports...'), and the topic match should be visible so I can see it does not concern sleep and grades.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename 'What the papers agree on' to 'What the papers report', and show the number of papers behind each statement. Show 'matched on: sleep apnea' when the topic match comes from a single incidental term.

findings.what_happened: The Sleep query showed 'PubMed 9,245 papers match' before the run and 'Ran: PubMed 38 · OpenAlex 412' afterwards. The Grades and Measurement queries show identical results (PubMed 2,207 / OpenAlex 451). The earlier banner says the counts are recorded samples, but the figures contradict each other on adjacent screens.
findings.expected: Either the counts agree or the difference is explained ('9,245 match; the 40 most relevant were collected, 38 fetched').
findings.suggested_fix: Label the figures as 'papers matching' and 'papers collected' in the same row, and explain 'collected' next to the 'Broad: only the 40 most relevant will be collected' warning.

findings.what_happened: Study type and article type both include 'review' wording ('Systematic / scoping review' vs 'Review article') and nothing explains the difference. Choosing Trial plus Review article returned 'Showing 0 of 158' while every chip kept its original count, so it looked like a bug until I reset.
findings.expected: A one-line explanation of 'article type = what kind of publication; study type = how the research was done'. Counts on the other chips should update, or the empty result should say that no paper is both.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a short tooltip or helper line above the two chip rows, and show 'No paper is both a Trial and a Review article' when the combination is empty.

findings.what_happened: Study-type counts on step 4 (Not reported 141, Other design 8, Trial 5) change on step 5 (Not reported 20, Other design 59, Cross-sectional 27, Qualitative 29). A note says the AI reads the abstracts next, but the first set looks like facts and the second contradicts it.
findings.expected: The step 4 chart should be labelled as 'database labels only' prominently, or show the 'unknown' category in an unmistakably provisional style.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename the step 4 heading to 'Study type (as labelled by the database; most are unlabelled)' and move the explanation above the bars.

findings.what_happened: The 3D scatter has no readable axis labels beyond 'Year', and 'Height has no meaning yet'. A hover-only point meaning and a rotating view are hard for keyboard users and beginners; the useful 'Show as 2D chart' checkbox is small. The green cross and teal-green triangle are close in hue.
findings.expected: The default for beginners is a 2D chart with a visible way to identify a paper.
findings.suggested_fix: Make 2D the default or put the toggle next to the chart title. Separate the two green hues further or rely on shape in the legend with bigger glyphs.

findings.what_happened: The first view of a new project has two buttons for the same action ('Sharpen my idea' on the card and 'Open step 1' in the top banner), and the card is called 'Idea' while the page says step 2 'Scoping'. The Demo banner says 'results will not match your topic' without saying what I should do about it.
findings.expected: One obvious next button, and demo text that tells a student what to do.
findings.suggested_fix: Hide the card button while the 'next step' banner is shown, or make both open the same panel. Add 'Click through to see how it works' to the demo banner.

findings.what_happened: The list says 'Keep', 'Edit', 'Delete' while the canvas cards say 'Accept' and 'Dismiss'. 'Measurement and outcomes' appeared as a topic with no link to my answer about grades. The page promised 4-8 topics but offered 4 and the 'which kinds of studies' question was never asked ('not answered yet').
findings.expected: One verb for the same action, topics that I recognise from my answers, and a note that skipped questions use defaults.
findings.suggested_fix: Use 'Keep' and 'Delete' everywhere. Add 'Why this topic?' under each topic. Show 'Study types: any (you can change this in step 3)' when not answered.

findings.what_happened: The 'Before you continue' checklist ticks 'Keep 3-5 papers per topic, or every matching paper where fewer match' as done even though the warning above says three topics have too few papers. The 'Appraise selected papers' confirmation dialog appeared 5+ seconds after my click and was easy to miss; I waited on the spinner-less page.
findings.expected: The checklist should not show a warning topic as done, and the dialog should appear immediately and take focus.
findings.suggested_fix: Tie the third checklist item to the warning state. Move focus into the dialog as soon as it opens.

findings.what_happened: PICo and PECO are named without explanation and 'Gap it fills' text is generic. Candidate 1 ('How do university students experience sleep?') drops grades, the second half of my idea. The 'Choose this question' / 'Chosen' / 'Edit this question' flow worked, but I could not tell what 'Finish and export' locked in.
findings.expected: A beginner-level line on what PECO means, and candidates that keep both parts of the original idea or say why one was dropped.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'PECO = Population, Exposure, Comparison, Outcome: a checklist for a good question' as a tooltip, and a one-line 'Why this question' linking back to the idea.

findings.what_happened: When the whole canvas is fitted to view, text on the nodes is about 7px and unreadable, and Topic and Query nodes share the same names ('Sleep', 'Sleep'). The helper also reported no visible focus on the panel heading.
findings.expected: A zoom level at which node titles are readable, and Topic/Query nodes that can be told apart by title.
findings.suggested_fix: Set a minimum zoom on Fit view or hide small text and show the step name only. Rename Query nodes to 'Search: Sleep'.

findings.what_happened: The 'Open printable report' link opens a new tab, which my helper could not follow, and the in-page preview is a small scroll box ('first 40 of 509 lines', then 'first 200 of 510 lines'). The line count changed by one between two previews, and the Report card text 'Markdown, a text file to edit or keep; to read, print or save it as PDF, open the printable report' is a long sentence for a beginner.
findings.expected: A single obvious way to read the report in full, and a stable line count.
findings.suggested_fix: Shorten the format labels ('Report (read and print)', 'Papers spreadsheet', 'Reference list') and make the printable report the primary button.

findings.page: Step 7 Appraisal (quote check and Show source)
findings.what_happened: On paper 1, a post-stroke telehealth meta-analysis, the first quote reads 'TITLE Patient satisfaction with telemedicine in the Philippines...'. That is a different paper. Show source displays that other paper's text with the quote highlighted, and the badge says 'found word for word'. The AI answer for the quality question was 'Unclear'.
findings.expected: A quote is checked only against the text of the paper it is attached to. A quote from another paper should show as 'not found'. At the least, the badge should not give false assurance.
findings.suggested_fix: Verify each quote against that paper's own full text or abstract id. Show the paper title above the source text. In demo mode, make the scripted quotes belong to the paper they are attached to, or label this check '(mock)' prominently. Add a test that fails if source-text paper id differs from the appraised paper id.

findings.page: Step 9 Research question (Full reasoning and quotes)
findings.what_happened: The chosen question, an effect of mindfulness on burnout in ICU nurses, shows a green 'found' supporting chip 'Ni'mah et al. 2023 · limitation' for the gap statement 'few included papers compare mindfulness-based interventions with usual care'. None of the included papers is about mindfulness, burnout or ICU nurses. The same chip is cited in the report as the gap's source.
findings.expected: A gap statement is backed by a quote that actually shows the claimed gap, or the app says that no included paper supports it. The report should not cite an unrelated telehealth paper as evidence for a mindfulness gap.
findings.suggested_fix: If the supporting quote's paper is not matched to any of the question's PICO terms, show 'No included paper supports this gap' instead of a green chip. In the report, label gaps with zero topic-matching evidence as unsupported.

findings.what_happened: For 'ICU nurses' the top-ranked papers are a post-stroke telehealth meta-analysis (score 72), immunotherapy in Asia, and Indonesian digital-health law, and they are called papers that 'match' the topic. Burnout, the main outcome, has 0 matching papers. A key finding is just a postal address ('Sutami 36A, Surakarta 57126...'). Another is just a trial number ('NCT07198828').
findings.expected: Matching and scoring should visibly reflect relevance to the topic, and the key-finding cell should hold a finding. Where it cannot, it should say 'no finding extracted'. Demo mode explains the topic mismatch but not a garbage extraction.
findings.suggested_fix: Show the matched terms for each paper in the 'why it scored' row. Reject key-finding text that has no result-like content (addresses, registry ids) and show 'not reported'. State in the demo banner on step 6 that rankings are scripted and not based on your topic.

findings.what_happened: The header counts '3 conflicts'. The conflict text itself says 'the demo sets two findings from different papers side by side... Read both quotes before treating this as a real disagreement.' The Known statements are about telemedicine in Southeast Asia, so they would be meaningless for a nursing dissertation.
findings.expected: A count of conflicts should only include real, checked disagreements. Otherwise it should be called 'possible conflicts'.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename to 'possible conflicts to check'. Do not count scripted or unchecked pairs in the headline number.

findings.what_happened: I clicked 'Write the searches'. The canvas gained query nodes, but the side panel stayed on 'Edit this search topic', labelled 'Viewing step 2 of 9 · Scoping · Done', and the footer button changed to 'Run all 8 searches' before I had seen a single search. I only saw the real searches after clicking 'Open step 3' on the canvas.
findings.expected: After 'Write the searches' the panel moves to the 'Check the searches before they run' view with the PubMed and OpenAlex blocks.
findings.suggested_fix: Switch the panel to the first query node automatically when the searches are written. If it must stay on the topic, show a 'Go to step 3' primary button as the intent doc describes.

findings.what_happened: The checklist item 'Keep 3-5 papers per topic, or every matching paper where fewer match' is ticked as done, while the same page warns that Burnout has none and two topics have only 2. The item 'Pick a topic' ticked itself after I merely clicked a topic tab.
findings.expected: Checklist ticks reflect what the user actually accomplished, and a warning state should not show as done.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not auto-tick the 3-5 item when any topic has fewer than 3 selected papers. Show it as 'needs attention'.

findings.what_happened: After typing my idea on /s/new I land on a second 'Check your idea, then start' screen showing the same text, which asks for another click on 'Sharpen my idea'. Question 1 then asks 'Who do you want to study?' although my idea says ICU nurses and the panel already shows 'ICU nurses'. There is no clear 'Skip the rest' until you are in the chat.
findings.expected: After 'Start my review' the user goes straight to the first useful question. Questions already answered by the idea are skipped.
findings.suggested_fix: Merge the idea-confirm screen into /s/new, or auto-start scoping. Pre-fill or skip questions whose slot is already filled from the idea.

findings.what_happened: Topic cards say '3 synonyms · 0 MeSH' and the field is 'Controlled vocabulary (MeSH)' showing 'none'. I do not know what MeSH is, and a zero looks like a failure. 'Mindfulness' is an actual MeSH heading, yet it is empty. The synonym list repeats the topic name itself, and 'Burnout' has only 1 synonym. The topic cards say 'Done' while Step 3 says 'Not started'. 'Measurement and outcomes' is vague as a search topic.
findings.expected: Plain wording such as 'official PubMed keywords: none added' with a short hint. Synonyms are new words. Topic cards say 'Approved' rather than 'Done' before step 3.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'MeSH' on the cards with 'PubMed keywords' plus a tooltip. Drop the topic name from the synonyms list. Use 'Approved' for the topic card status.

findings.what_happened: Counts do not reconcile for a user. 'Burnout' and 'Measurement and outcomes' both show exactly PubMed 8,058. Per-search counts add up to about 28,000, yet the source bars say 'PubMed 5 fetched · OpenAlex 135 fetched'. The text says '140 fetched, 21 duplicates' but the per-query labels give no fetched numbers.
findings.expected: Each query card says matches found vs records collected (for example 'found 8,058, collected 40') so the numbers do not look contradictory.
findings.suggested_fix: On query nodes show 'N matches, 40 collected'. Label the large numbers 'matches in database' and the other 'records we collected'.

findings.what_happened: At retrieval, 116 of 119 papers are grey 'Not reported' circles, so the chart conveys almost nothing. In the ranking map with a topic selected, the legend says 'Other design 25' but I see only 2 plus signs: papers not selected for appraisal are faded to near-invisibility. The caption 'Height has no meaning yet' is odd. Legend entries with zero papers (Trial, Cohort, Cross-sectional) show no count.
findings.expected: Faded points are still visible, with a legend line such as 'faded = not selected (34)'. Zero counts are shown as 0.
findings.suggested_fix: Raise the faded opacity to a visible minimum and add a legend entry for faded points. Show '0' for empty categories. At step 4 hide or explain the chart when most papers have no label.

findings.what_happened: The primary export button says 'Download Markdown' and the card says 'Markdown, a text file'. I do not know what Markdown is, and I want a PDF or Word file. The PDF route is a secondary button, 'Open printable report', which opens in a new tab. The chosen question is exported with a '(mock)' prefix that I would have to remove by hand. The selected radio card's description text is dim grey.
findings.expected: A first-time user sees 'Download report (PDF or Word)' or at least 'Open printable report to save as PDF' as the main action. The question text is editable before export without a mock prefix.
findings.suggested_fix: Make 'Open printable report (save as PDF)' the primary button, or offer a PDF/DOCX download. Rename 'Markdown' to 'Editable text file'. Raise the contrast of the selected card's description.

findings.what_happened: The 'Start my review' button looks fully active (bright blue) while the page says 'Write at least a sentence to start' and the control is disabled. I could not tell from the screenshot that it was disabled until I typed.
findings.expected: A disabled button looks disabled, or an enabled button explains the missing input on click.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the disabled state a clearly muted style, or keep it enabled and show the hint on click.

findings.what_happened: The side panel covers about half the canvas, so nodes are cropped (topic cards and queries cut off at the right edge) and the canvas does not re-fit to the visible area. Tabs in the synthesis panel are cut off ('M...'). Step 1 offers both 'Open step 1' and 'Sharpen my idea', which look like the same action.
findings.expected: The canvas re-centres on the active node when the panel opens, and tabs wrap or scroll with a visible cue.
findings.suggested_fix: Fit the view to the visible area when the panel opens. Add scroll arrows or wrap the topic tabs. Show only one primary button on the Idea node.

findings.what_happened: The 'See a review take shape' animation is cropped on the left, leaves the right two thirds empty, and shows an unrelated example (adoption, policy and governance, digital infrastructure) with large counts and a spinner. It is not obvious what it shows. The headline is long.
findings.expected: The animation is centred and fits its frame.
findings.suggested_fix: Centre or scale the animation to its container and add a one-line caption.

reports.categories_and_colours: I could find and filter by study type and by article type in three places: the retrieval panel (article-type bars you click to filter the chart), the step 5/6 table (chips for both, with counts), and the map legend. Study type has 7 values (Trial, Cohort / case-control, Cross-sectional, Qualitative / mixed methods, Systematic / scoping review, Other design, Not reported). Each has its own colour and shape: blue circle, orange square, teal triangle, gold diamond, pink star, green plus, grey ring. Without being told, I understood from the chip row that colour and shape show the kind of study, and that clicking one shows only that kind. Article type is plain grey chips with no colour, which avoids reusing colours. Filtering worked and was honest ('showing 14 of 119: review article, 105 hidden from the chart (still in the review)', with Show all). Counts matched between table chips and legend (for example 23 qualitative, 56 other design). Problems: at retrieval the study type comes only from the databases, so 116 of 119 are 'Not reported' and the chart is a field of identical grey circles. Study-type counts then change completely at step 5 (Not reported 116 becomes 14, Other design 3 becomes 56). The page does explain this, but it is startling. 'Other design' is a large vague bucket (56). In the ranking map, faded 'not selected' papers are almost invisible, so legend counts such as 'Other design 25' do not match the dots visible. Legend entries with zero papers show no number. The 3D/2D chart is small inside the side panel. Colour-by 'Topic' and 'Source' exist but I did not use them.
reports.validity_assessment: Honesty about the demo is very strong. A dismissible banner says scripted AI and recorded telemedicine papers. AI text is prefixed '(mock)'. The report opens with 'not a real review' and 'a scoping aid, not an exhaustive systematic search'. Single-reviewer selection is stated. The novelty check says plainly that finding no similar study does not prove novelty, and no 'novel' claim appears anywhere. There are explicit gates for thin evidence: the amber step 6 warning, the 'Appraise anyway' dialog, 'No evidence for Burnout... this review can say nothing about it' at step 8, and the '7 quotes not decided yet' dialog. Traceability machinery is good: PICO breakdown, quote chips, Show source with highlights, a 'found word for word' versus 'you decide' state, and the report counting found and rejected quotes. However, in this run the traceability is not trustworthy. A quote attached to a post-stroke meta-analysis was verified 'found word for word' against a different (Philippines) paper's text. The gap for my chosen question cites an unrelated telehealth paper through a green 'found' chip. Papers 'matching' ICU nurses were about post-stroke telehealth and immunotherapy. Key findings included a postal address and a trial number. A question about mindfulness and burnout was drafted with zero papers on either. These mismatches are explained by demo mode only partly: the app says the topic will not match, but the green 'found' badges still imply support that is not there. For a real run, the verification of quotes against the right paper's text must be checked, since the demo shows a quote check that can pass on the wrong source. Overall I would judge the structure of the workflow valid and traceable by design, and the demo honest, but one badge ('found word for word') is not reliable as built.
reports.would_have_quit_at: I would not have quit, as the flow never blocks and every step has one clear main button. My patience ran lowest at step 7 (Appraisal), where the paragraph of explanation, the three checklist items and 7 undecided quotes slow me down, and at step 3, where 'Write the searches' appeared to do nothing in the panel. Trust would break for real at step 7 or step 9 if I noticed that the quote verified as 'found word for word' came from a different paper. If this were a real run rather than a demo, I would stop and not use the question for my proposal.

reports.narrative: I landed, saw the headline, and clicked the blue Start a review. Signup was quick. I typed my topic and kept clicking the obvious button. The first thing that annoyed me was that I typed my idea and was then asked to confirm the same idea on another screen. Then the first scoping question asked who I want to study, although I had written ICU nurses. I answered once, then hit Skip the rest. The four suggested topics were sensible. I did not know what '0 MeSH' meant. At step 3 I clicked Write the searches and nothing seemed to happen in the panel until I found Open step 3 on the canvas. Then the searches were readable, and Run all 8 searches finished in seconds. The retrieval sentence about duplicates is the clearest thing in the app. The table with coloured shape chips was easy, and I could filter by study type and article type without any help. At step 6 the amber warning told me Burnout had no papers, which scared me, and it also made me trust the app. Step 7 was heavy. I skipped the 7 undecided quotes. When I clicked Show source I noticed that the highlighted text was about the Philippines, while the paper I was reading was about post-stroke patients, yet it said found word for word. That damaged my trust. I still reached step 9, picked the PICO question, and downloaded Markdown. I did not know what Markdown is and wanted a PDF. The banner kept saying demo mode, which was honest, but my whole review was about telemedicine in Southeast Asia, so I could not use any of it.

findings.what_happened: The demo corpus is telemedicine and mHealth in Southeast Asia, yet off-topic papers get absolute scores of 63-68 out of 100. Rank 1 is an mHealth review of the Western Pacific. 'Topic fit 3/5' is given for '2 topic terms appear'. The only relevance alert is the amber 'Long COVID: only 1 matches' banner. Scores do not signal that nothing in the list is really on topic.
findings.expected: A score that stays low, or an explicit 'no paper is a good match' alert, when every candidate is off-topic. A reviewer could be misled into thinking a 68/100 paper is a decent match.
findings.suggested_fix: Show the topic-fit sub-score as its own column and add a 'weak match' flag when topic fit is below a threshold. Do not let recency or citation points lift an irrelevant paper to a mid-range total.

findings.what_happened: After I edited and kept 'Long COVID', I clicked the text 'Return-to-work outcomes'. The topic vanished, the list dropped to '3 topics, aim for 4-8', and a live region announced 'Topic deleted.' No confirmation was asked and no Undo was visible. I cannot be certain which element my click resolved to, but a single click on a topic name removed it.
findings.expected: Deleting a topic needs an explicit Delete press with confirmation, or a visible Undo, as quotes have. Clicking a name should only select it.
findings.suggested_fix: Make deletion require the explicit Delete button with an Undo toast, and ensure the Delete control's accessible name or hit area cannot be triggered by clicking the topic label.

findings.what_happened: The generated query is a recorded example. Group 1 uses only 4 of my 7 synonyms, my MeSH term was not included, and the 2020-now date limit is not in the string. The 'Long COVID' query already ANDs in the return-to-work terms, so each topic query is not that topic alone. There is no single combined population AND exposure AND outcome string. My hand-edited string (with [Mesh], 7 synonyms, a worker concept) was parsed back into labelled chips with an 'edited by you' badge, which works well. The banner does say demo searches 'do not follow your edits'.
findings.expected: The generated string should visibly use every synonym and MeSH term I defined. It should also make clear how topics are combined into the final strategy.
findings.suggested_fix: Generate the string from the topic's full synonym and MeSH list, show a one-line 'how topics are combined' explanation, and print the final combined strategy for each database in the report.

findings.what_happened: I deselected 'Enhancing human and animal health data integration...' under the Return-to-work topic ('13 selected' stayed 13 after swapping in another paper). In step 7 that same paper appeared as 'Paper 1 of 11'. Probably it stayed selected under another topic, but nothing explains this, and 13 selected became 11 appraised without a reason.
findings.expected: Either a swap is global, or the page says 'still selected for topic X' and explains why 13 selected became 11 papers appraised.
findings.suggested_fix: Show which topics a paper is selected for, warn when a deselect only applies to one topic, and explain the selected-to-appraised count change.

findings.what_happened: Counts are inconsistent. My edited Long COVID query 'matched 8,058' in PubMed, but the run record says 'Ran: PubMed 979'. Two different topic queries both report exactly 8,058. The report adds up 19,932 'hits' across searches. Also 'only the 40 most relevant will be collected', so the corpus is a capped sample. It is disclosed in step 3 and the report, but not on the retrieval summary or landing page.
findings.expected: A match count for a query should be stable and distinct per query, and the cap should sit beside the '114 different papers' headline.
findings.suggested_fix: Show one count per query and per database, state '40 collected per search' next to the retrieval total, and drop the meaningless summed hits figure.

findings.what_happened: I answered 4 questions (who, where, outcome, years). The card then said '5 of 5 questions' and went straight to 'Suggest search topics'. The 'Which kinds of studies' field stayed 'not answered yet', so my study-design criteria were never captured. The panel says '5 of 6 answered' while the card says '5 of 5'.
findings.expected: The study-design question should be asked, and the question counters should agree.
findings.suggested_fix: Ask all five scoping questions or label the counts consistently. Prompt for study design before moving on, because eligibility needs it.

findings.what_happened: After 'Write the searches', the side panel kept showing the topic editor with the header 'Viewing step 2 of 9, Scoping' while the strip said step 3. Topic cards say 'Done' while the step is 'Not started'. After 'Keep this topic' the card still said 'Your turn' with 'Edit this search topic', so I could not tell if it was kept. On the canvas, query cards did not open from a click and I had to switch to List to read the query.
findings.expected: One clear state per card. After writing searches, the panel should show the queries.
findings.suggested_fix: Auto-open the first query after 'Write the searches', and use one status vocabulary (Suggested, Kept, Your turn) across card and panel.

findings.what_happened: Quote checks are visible and traceable. 'Show source' highlights the quote in the text, with a closest-passage diff when not found, and the report counts quotes. But the first 'Aim' quote spans 'TITLE ... ABSTRACT' headers and stops mid-sentence, so 'found word for word' is weak. A trial protocol is appraised for 'Key findings'. Each paper carries one planted altered quote ('clearly proves the intervention works everywhere'), and 5 stayed undecided.
findings.expected: Quotes should be complete sentences from the body, and protocols should not be asked for findings.
findings.suggested_fix: Strip TITLE/ABSTRACT scaffolding, end quotes on sentence boundaries, and skip the findings checklist for protocols. Keep the closest-passage view.

findings.what_happened: Known statements are the quote pasted in, truncated with an ellipsis, so this is quote-listing and not synthesis. The first 'Known' statement under the Long COVID tab is about teleconsultation. Chips link to quotes and each states 'found, not proof', which is good traceability.
findings.expected: A statement should paraphrase and cite, and flag when the cited paper is not about the topic.
findings.suggested_fix: Generate a one-sentence paraphrase with the quote as evidence, and add an 'off-topic source' flag when topic fit is low.

findings.what_happened: I rewrote the question to ask about 'time to sustained return to work', which implies a longitudinal cohort. The report still says 'Design: Cross-sectional survey', and the mock Gap, Feasibility and Weakness text (with a citation to Tran et al. 2025) is carried over onto my new wording. Candidate 3 reads 'What helps or hinders long COVID', which is ambiguous.
findings.expected: Editing the question should flag that design, gap and weakness may no longer fit, or let me update them.
findings.suggested_fix: After an edit, mark gap, feasibility and weakness as 'written for the previous wording' and offer to regenerate them.

findings.what_happened: The rubric is fully visible (topic fit 35, design 20, setting 20, recency 15, citations 10), which I value. But the weights cannot be edited. Three criteria are 'scored by the AI from title and abstract', yet a paper's reason says '(mock) Keyword-overlap score'. Citation count is used as a quality proxy, and no formal risk-of-bias tool is used.
findings.expected: The way each score is produced should be stated consistently, and I would like adjustable weights or the option to switch citation impact off.
findings.suggested_fix: Let users adjust or disable weights, state per criterion whether it is AI-scored or a formula, and name the appraisal tool used.

findings.what_happened: The landing page says it 'finds real papers' and every quote is 'checked against its source', and sign-up never mentions demo mode or that the output is 'a scoping aid, not an exhaustive systematic search' (the report says so). The demo banner first appears after sign-up, and the 40-paper cap is not mentioned. A sceptical reviewer sees the honest limits only deep inside the flow.
findings.expected: A one-line scoping-aid statement near the main claim, and a demo-mode notice on public pages.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'A scoping aid, not an exhaustive systematic search' under the hero text, and show the demo note on landing and sign-up when the server is in demo mode.

findings.what_happened: 'Start my review' and 'Create account' look fully active in the screenshots, but the helper reports them as 'looks disabled'. three_second_test.note: A guided tool that turns a rough idea into a research question backed by real papers. First action is Start a review, next is sign up. Clear. The 'What Athena will not do' list answers my first doubts.
An account form, so I fill email and password. Focus lands on Email rather than the first field. Button looks active though a helper hint reads disabled.
Describe my idea in a sentence or two, then press Start my review. Example chips help.
A map of my review with one card and a 9-step strip. Two buttons seem to do the same thing (Sharpen my idea and Open step 1). The demo banner is clear.
A short interview that turns my idea into search topics. I type an answer and send. The live 'what we know so far' echoes my words, which builds trust.
Keep, edit or delete each suggested topic. The vague 'Measurement and outcomes' topic stands out and I can fix it.
After writing the searches the panel still showed the topic editor labelled 'step 2'. I had to hunt for the queries and could only read them from List view.
Concept blocks as chips, a Count matches button, and an editable raw string behind 'Edit the search text'. Demo caveat is stated.
'190 fetched, 76 duplicates, 114 different papers remain.' Clear PRISMA-style numbers and a mix chart.
One row per paper, AI-drafted from abstract only, with a 3-item checklist and study and article type filters.
Check which papers go forward, with score bars and a Keep checkbox. The amber warning about a topic with one match is clear.
Go paper by paper, check the AI answers and decide quotes the check could not find. Dense but well explained; found is not proof.
Known, contested and unknown statements with quote chips and conflicts per topic tab.
Pick one of three candidates with gap, feasibility, weakness and a PICo or PECO structure. Novelty caveat is explicit.
Download the report, spreadsheet or reference list. Each format has a plain-language note.

reports.categories_and_colours: I found both category systems without being told. Retrieval shows 'Article type (from the databases)' bars in neutral grey for journal article, review article, preprint, editorial and other, and a separate 'Study type' list with colour AND shape: blue circle for trial, orange square for cohort or case-control, green triangle for cross-sectional, amber diamond for qualitative or mixed methods, pink star for systematic or scoping review, green plus for other design, and a hollow grey ring for not reported. The key says 'hover or focus to highlight, click to show only that category'. I clicked and it filtered, and the lines 'Showing only one category (1 papers)' and 'Showing 6 of 114: systematic / scoping review; review article. 108 papers are hidden by your filters (still in the review)' confirmed that filters are views and not deletions, with Reset filters always visible. Shape plus label means colour is never the only cue. A Colour by selector exists on the map, and there is a 2D toggle for the 3D scatter. Weaknesses: 102 of 114 papers are 'Not reported' at retrieval, which makes the study-type colours nearly meaningless until step 5. Counts change between steps (Trial 4 to 6, Systematic review 1 to 9) without an on-chip explanation. The 3D chart says 'Height has no meaning yet'. Green appears on two shapes (triangle and plus), distinguished only by shape. The legend lists unused categories greyed out. Article type and study type are two similar-looking filter rows, so 'Review article 13' versus 'Systematic / scoping review 9' needs a moment's thought.
reports.validity_assessment: As a rigour-minded reviewer I would call this app an unusually honest scoping aid, and traceable in its mechanics, but not something I could defend as a systematic review. Traceability is strong. Search syntax is visible and editable (my hand-written [Mesh] and [tiab] string was parsed back into labelled chips with an 'edited by you' badge). Each rank score has a per-criterion reason and formula. Quotes can be opened against the source text with a highlight, and failed quotes show the closest passage and need my decision (I rejected 11, 5 stayed undecided and were excluded by default). The report preamble states plainly: 'a scoping aid, not an exhaustive systematic search', up to 40 records per search, a single reviewer, 93 quotes found, 16 not found with my accept and reject counts, and 'a found quote shows the words are in the paper, not that they prove the claim'. Novelty is not overclaimed: 'Finding no similar study does not prove a question is new.' Gates warn when a topic has fewer than 3 papers or quotes are undecided. Nothing looked fabricated: every appraised paper showed a DOI and came from a database record. Weaknesses: in demo mode the whole corpus is off-topic, so I could not judge real relevance or retrieval quality; I could not confirm that real mode honours my synonyms, MeSH, dates or edited query (the demo banner says it does not). Off-topic papers score 63-68 of 100, which could mislead. Synthesis is quote-listing and not synthesis. Deselecting a paper under one topic did not remove it from appraisal, and counts were inconsistent (8,058 vs 979). There is no formal risk-of-bias tool, no second-reviewer process, no adjustable rubric, and the capped 40-record retrieval means no completeness claim is possible. I could not read the report's full search-strategy section, so I do not know whether my edited query is recorded verbatim. Net: defensible as a documented, auditable scoping exercise, not as a systematic review, and the app mostly says so itself.
reports.would_have_quit_at: I would not have quit: I reached the exported report. Where I would have stopped trusting it in a real run: the Search builder (step 3), because the generated PubMed string omitted my MeSH term and 3 of 7 synonyms and mixed topics, so I would rewrite each string by hand and could not verify real mode honours that. I would also have paused at Ranking (step 6) when a deselected paper reappeared in Appraisal, and I would not present the Synthesis statements to my committee as they are quote pastes.

reports.narrative: I arrived expecting an AI tool to bluff, and the landing page's 'What Athena will not do' list, with no invented references and a full-text-versus-abstract disclosure, made me curious. Sign-up was easy. The demo banner only appeared after sign-up, which I would have liked earlier. The scoping questions felt like a real supervisor chat, though it stopped after four and never asked about study design. In topics I edited synonyms and MeSH, then somehow deleted a topic by clicking its name with no confirmation, which annoyed me. Step 3 was my favourite: I could read the exact PubMed string, rewrite it, and watch it parse back into labelled chips. But the generated version skipped my MeSH term and several synonyms, and the counts (8,058 versus 979) did not add up. Retrieval gave me clean PRISMA-style numbers. The study type and article type filters worked, and the shape-plus-colour key was readable. In ranking, every score exposed its reasoning, but off-topic telemedicine papers still scored 68 out of 100. I swapped a paper and it later reappeared in appraisal, which shook me a little. Appraisal impressed me most. 'Show source' highlights quotes in the text, and altered quotes like 'clearly proves the intervention works everywhere' were flagged for me to reject. The synthesis was weaker, just truncated quotes. The candidate questions came with PECO structure and an explicit 'no similar study does not prove novelty' line. The exported report says it is a scoping aid, not a systematic review, which is what I wanted to read. I would use it for scoping, not as my review.

findings.what_happened: The first paper is 'Community nursing services during the COVID-19 pandemic: the Singapore experience', but its first quote starts 'TITLE Telemedicine Guidelines in South East Asia A Scoping Review ABSTRACT ...' and is stamped 'found word for word'. Show source highlights that text as the paper's full text. The attached full text belongs to a different paper, and the check cannot tell.
findings.expected: Quotes and source text should come from the paper named in the heading, or the app should warn that the text does not match the title or DOI.
findings.suggested_fix: Verify that the retrieved full text's title or DOI matches the paper record before running the quote check. Show a visible 'text may belong to another paper' warning if not, and make the demo fixtures match their papers.

findings.what_happened: The Retrieval query card says 'Hip fracture surgery: PubMed 979 · OpenAlex 707', which looks like plenty of hits. Later, Ranking and Synthesis say 'no papers match' and 'no papers were found for it'. A clinician cannot tell why 1,686 hits became zero papers. The 135 fetched and 71 unique papers vs the 9,245 counts is also not explained, and the text mixes '8 searches' with 'from 4 queries'.
findings.expected: One consistent story: say that only the first N records per search are fetched, and say plainly that none of the fetched papers matched this topic's words.
findings.suggested_fix: Show 'matches in database' vs 'fetched' vs 'matched this topic' for each query. Reword the synthesis warning to 'none of the N papers we fetched for this topic were about it'. Use one word, 'searches', everywhere.

findings.what_happened: The candidate research questions end with a truncated word: 'surgical repair of a hip fract'. Candidate 2 is also repetitive: 'recovery after hip fracture surgery among adults aged 65 and over after surgical repair of a hip fract?'. These are the questions the user is meant to choose and export. The Population field also holds the truncated phrase.
findings.expected: Complete, grammatical question text with no cut-off words.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not character-truncate a population phrase when building candidate wording. Truncate at word boundaries or not at all, and avoid repeating the topic in the sentence.

findings.what_happened: A paper on perinatal mental telehealth in Singapore scores 64 and is auto-selected, and 9 papers are selected in total. Not one is about hip fracture, older adults or rehabilitation. The score looks authoritative, and the paper detail pane does not show why it scored 64, although the checklist says 'Open a selected paper to see why it scored high'. Demo mode is announced, so this is honest overall, but the score itself carries no relevance warning.
findings.expected: Open a selected paper to see a per-criterion score breakdown, and a low-relevance flag when a paper does not match the question.
findings.suggested_fix: Show the five rubric scores in the paper details, and cap or flag the overall score when topic match is low. Make the checklist text match what the pane shows.

findings.what_happened: 'The LvL UP trial: Protocol for a ... randomised controlled trial' is labelled 'Trial', but it is only a protocol with no results. A protocol also shows the registry number 'NCT07198828' as its 'key finding'. The detail view calls another paper 'Narrative review' while the list says 'Other design'.
findings.expected: Protocols should count as 'Other design', and key finding should be a finding.
findings.suggested_fix: Classify protocols as Other design. Do not accept an identifier as a key finding. Show the same study-type vocabulary in the list and the details.

findings.what_happened: The orange 'Few papers match 2 topics' warning is clipped at the right edge. Sentences are cut off ('are already selected ... not'). The 'Edit the searches for Walking ability and function (step 3)' button overflows the box and is truncated.
findings.expected: Text wraps inside the box and buttons stay within the viewport at 375px.
findings.suggested_fix: Allow the warning's content and buttons to wrap (min-width:0, flex-wrap, full-width buttons on narrow screens).

findings.what_happened: A quote is flagged 'not found, you decide', yet the 'closest passage' shown is word-for-word identical to the quote, with the note 'same words, but not in this order or form'. A user cannot see why it failed and does not know whether to accept it.
findings.expected: A clear reason for the mismatch, for example 'differs only in spacing or line breaks', or an automatic pass.
findings.evidence: docs/qa/iteration-3/clinician/16j.jpg (paper 7, first quote, 'Data analysis sufficiently rigorous')
findings.suggested_fix: Normalise whitespace, hyphenation and case before matching. If still flagged, highlight the differing characters.

findings.what_happened: In the edit form the question textarea gets focus but has an empty accessible name, and the 'Question' label is not bound to it. The browser helper's fill by label 'Question' hit a non-input, while Population and Outcome worked. Shift+Tab from Population skipped the textarea and landed on 'What happens in this step'.
findings.expected: Every field has a programmatic label, and tab order follows the visual order.
findings.suggested_fix: Use <label for> or aria-label on the question textarea and check the DOM and tab order of the edit form.

findings.what_happened: I wanted to email the report to myself from a phone. There is no email or share button. The default format is a Markdown text file, which a phone cannot open easily. The nicer 'printable report' opens in a new tab and the button sits above the radio list, so it is unclear whether it is the same thing as the Report option. After 'Download Markdown' only a small footer note confirms it.
findings.expected: A phone-friendly route: share or email the report, or a PDF.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'Send to my email' or the native share sheet, and make PDF or the readable report the default on phones. Say that the printable report and the Markdown file hold the same content.

three_second_test.note: For: turning a rough idea into a research question backed by real papers. First: read the headline. Next: tap 'Start a review'. Clear and calm. The 'What Athena will not do' accordion is reassuring. Demo mode is not mentioned on the landing page, only inside the app.
Create an account with name, email and password, then tap 'Create account'. The password rule is shown. Nothing confusing.
Describe my research idea. Type a sentence or tap an example, then 'Start my review'. The button looks active while disabled.
A list of my idea at step 1, with a 'Your next step' bar and the demo banner. Tap 'Open step 1'. Slightly redundant after pressing Start.
Answer up to 5 short questions about who, where and what. Type an answer, then 'Send answer'. 'What we know so far' updates as I answer. The header takes up too much space.
Keep or delete the suggested topics, then tap 'Keep N suggested topics'. The dashed and 'suggested' labels help. One topic name is garbled, and small Edit and Delete targets.

Check the PubMed and OpenAlex searches before running. Tap 'Run all 8 searches'. It took me a moment because the panel first showed a topic editor and I had to find the searches. The demo note is clear.
See how many papers were found and the mix of types, then tap 'Summarise the papers'. The big numbers (135 fetched, 64 duplicates, 71 papers) are clear, with bars that can be tapped to filter.
Skim the AI summaries and fix wrong cells, then 'Rank the papers'. The 3-item checklist is clear, but long before I reach the first paper on a phone.

Choose which papers go forward. First a topic chip, then 'Appraise selected papers'. The clipped warning box and scores without explanation slowed me. The warning that Hip fracture surgery has 0 papers is honest.
Go through each paper and decide on quotes marked 'not found'. 'Show only quotes I need to decide' then 'Next paper'. The red-flagged quote and the 'Accept anyway or Reject' choice are easy to grasp.
Read what is known, contested and unknown, with quote chips. Then 'Suggest research questions'. The 'No evidence for 1 topic' banner is excellent.
Compare three candidate questions and pick one; tapping a card chooses it. The novelty note is cautious. Truncated 'hip fract' wording hurts trust.
Download the review. Check the question and tap Download. As a phone user I wanted 'email to myself', which is not offered.

reports.categories_and_colours: I could find and filter papers by both study type and article type. In the retrieval step, bars for each article type (Journal article 52, Review article 7, Preprint 2, Editorial/letter/comment 9, Other publication 1) can be tapped to show only those papers. A check mark, 'Chart: showing 7 of 71: review article. 64 papers are hidden from the chart (still in the review). Show all' made the state obvious. The same filters appear as chips in the summary table (Trial 6, Cohort/case-control 1, Cross-sectional 15, Qualitative/mixed 15, Systematic/scoping review 5, Other design 14, Not reported 15) and ranking tables. Study type uses colour and shape together: Trial = blue circle, Cohort/case-control = orange square, Cross-sectional = green triangle, Qualitative/mixed = amber diamond, Systematic/scoping review = pink star, Other design = green cross, Not reported = grey ring. A legend with counts sits above the chart, zero-count types are dimmed, and the key says 'tap a category to show only that one'. I understood the colours without being told. Article type is plain bars without hues, so colour does not mean two things. Small problems: before AI summaries, 59 of 71 are 'Not reported' and after summaries only 15, which is explained ('the AI reads every abstract in the next step'); the legend counts stay at whole-corpus values when a filter is applied; the legend shows green twice (triangle and cross) and relies on shape to separate them; the protocol-as-Trial label and the 'Narrative review' vs 'Other design' wording; the chart is clipped at the left edge on a phone and its height axis 'has no meaning yet', which is honest but puzzling. I did not use 'Colour by' options besides study type.
reports.validity_assessment: Mostly honest, and the traceability design is strong, but it would not yet produce a valid review in this demo. Strengths: the demo banner is persistent and plain ('AI is scripted... recorded sample papers... results will not match your topic'); AI text is tagged '(mock)'; every paper has DOI, PMID, PMCID and OpenAlex ids; summaries are labelled 'AI · abstract'; appraisal quotes are checked word for word, with 'found word for word' vs 'not found, you decide', a highlighted source view and a nearest passage; a deliberately altered overclaim ('clearly proves the intervention works everywhere') was caught on every paper, and I could reject it, with rejected quotes excluded from the synthesis. The app says 'Found means the words are in the paper, not that they prove the answer'. It also states that 'Finding no similar study does not prove a question is new' and that the novelty check in demo mode says nothing about novelty. Warnings for topics with no evidence appear at ranking, in the confirmation dialog and in synthesis. Weaknesses: (1) a quote and source text came from a different paper than the title ('Telemedicine Guidelines in South East Asia' under a Singapore community nursing paper) yet passed as 'found word for word'; (2) none of the 9 selected papers concern hip fracture, yet they receive scores like 64 with no per-criterion explanation; (3) 979 and 707 hits for Hip fracture surgery contradict 'no papers were found'; (4) candidate questions contain truncated words ('hip fract'); (5) 'Unknown' shows limitations as gaps; (6) a protocol is labelled Trial; (7) a quote flagged 'not found' when the closest passage is identical. A real-mode run would need these traceability checks (title/DOI match, relevance flag) to be trustworthy. Nothing looked like a fabricated reference: all ids came from records, and the app never claimed novelty without a caveat.
reports.would_have_quit_at: I completed the whole journey and downloaded the report. A real busy physician would probably have quit at step 6 (Ranking). The page says that 'Hip fracture surgery' has no matching papers, only one paper matches 'Walking ability and function', and all selected papers are about other subjects. Around step 3 and 7 many taps and long panels on a phone also tempt abandonment: the extra 'Open step 1' and 'Sharpen' taps, the Search builder panel jumping back to the topic editor, and 10 quotes spread over 8 papers to decide one by one. Without email or share, the final report would have to be found in downloads, and the printable report opens in a new tab.
reports.activity: Created a new account (Dr Okafor, okafor.qa3@example.com). Created one project 'Does tele-rehabilitation help older adults recover after hip fracture surgery?' (prj_d635b3b1f4414481) and took it through all 9 steps to export. Answered 5 scoping questions, edited one topic (name and synonyms) and kept 4 topics, wrote and ran 8 searches (71 unique papers, 64 duplicates), summarised and ranked papers (9 selected, 'Appraise anyway' on a warning), decided 10 quotes (rejected 9 planted overclaims or off-topic quotes and accepted 1), generated synthesis (13 statements, 2 conflicts) and 3 candidate questions, chose candidate 2, edited its wording and outcome, then pressed 'Download Markdown' (download confirmed) and tried the printable report (opened in a new tab that my browser helper could not follow, so I could not read its content). The console and network were clean at every check ('no console errors or failed requests'). No AI errors, stuck spinners or lost inputs. About 130 helper commands; screenshots saved in docs/qa/iteration-3/clinician/. Read docs/ux-intent.md only after finishing.
reports.narrative: I opened Athena on my phone between rounds. The landing page told me in a few seconds what it does, so I tapped Start a review, signed up and typed my hip fracture question. Scoping was pleasant: five short questions and the topics took shape. One topic came out garbled ('Whether walking ability'), so I renamed it and rewrote its synonyms. I was a little annoyed by the extra Open step 1 and Sharpen taps after pressing Start, and the search step first showed me a topic editor instead of the searches. Retrieval was the best page for categories: clear counts, tappable article type bars, and a study-type legend using colour plus shape, which I understood at once. Ranking is where trust wobbled. The honest warning says nothing matches Hip fracture surgery, yet nine unrelated papers were selected with confident scores, and the warning box was clipped on the right. The demo banner explained why, which I appreciated. Appraisal impressed me: planted overclaims such as 'clearly proves the intervention works everywhere' were flagged, and I could reject them. However, the first quote and source text belonged to a different paper than the title. Synthesis linked each statement to a quote chip. I chose candidate 2 but the wording ended in 'hip fract', so I edited it. At export I wanted to email myself the report, but only a Markdown download and a new-tab printable report exist. I downloaded Markdown and the app confirmed it. Overall: honest and traceable, but long on a phone.

findings.what_happened: Quotes that have nothing to do with the checklist question get a green 'found word for word' tick. 'Attrition / loss to follow-up reported' is answered 'AI: Unclear' with a background sentence about mHealth preventing NCDs. 'Primary outcome pre-specified' shows a sentence about secondary outcomes. The tick only means the words exist in the paper. A reader with limited English will read a green tick as 'checked and OK'. The explanatory sentence sits far above the tick, at the top of the panel.
findings.expected: A tick that says 'the words exist' must not look like a tick that says 'this supports the answer'. Quotes that do not address the question should be marked 'does not answer this question'.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename the badge to 'Quote exists in paper' and use a neutral colour, not green. Add a second badge 'Relevant to this question? yes/unclear'. Repeat the caveat in a tooltip on every badge.

findings.what_happened: The 'Key findings' of a trial protocol is its abstract-background sentence. The 'Known' statements are about how another review was done (Arksey and O'Malley, PRISMA-ScR, Mendeley duplicates), not about diabetes or apps. Selected papers include 'Precision medicine in Thailand' and e-mental-health surveys. The three research questions are still drawn from this. The Gap field cites 'Sabrina et al. 2021 limitation', a telemedicine data-ownership note that has nothing to do with the gap named. The demo banner explains why, but the structure shows no check that a quote supports its statement.
findings.expected: A statement should be tied to a quote that is on topic, and protocols or reviews-of-methods should not be listed as findings. Even in demo mode the structure should show off-topic evidence honestly.
findings.suggested_fix: Label protocols 'no results yet'. Add 'does this quote support this statement?' per chip. Warn in synthesis when most statements are about methods, not results. Show a 'low relevance' badge when topic fit is below the threshold.

findings.what_happened: A Thai paper whose abstract says 'we conducted a narrative review of published literature' is labelled 'Cross-sectional' (triangle). The docs say narrative reviews belong in 'Other design'. The 'Study type' chips do not say these labels are AI-guessed, while the retrieval page said 'only where the database labels it'. Counts jump from 102 not reported at step 4 to 17 at step 5 with no explanation at the filter.
findings.expected: The study-type facet and legend should say 'AI-guessed from abstract' where counts changed. Obvious mismatches between abstract and label should be easy to spot and fix.
findings.suggested_fix: Put the 'AI · abstract' badge on the 'Study type' facet label too. Add a line 'Study type changed from database labels (6 trials) to AI reading (6 trials, 13 cross-sectional...)'. Flag rows where the abstract says 'review' but the type is not a review.

findings.what_happened: I added synonyms, and the app moved me back to step 2 with an amber 'Step 2 is open again' warning. I had to go back, press 'Use these topics' again, return to step 3 and press 'Write the searches'. A warning at the top of the page does say this, but a non-native reader skips it and cannot tell what 'reopens step 2' means. After 'Write the searches' the panel still showed the topic editor under 'Viewing step 2', with no cue to look at the new Query rows. The helper in the Docs says the single next action is 'Run all N searches', but 'Write the searches' is an extra step.
findings.expected: Editing a synonym should save without reopening an approved step, or the app should explain in one plain sentence what will happen before I type. After writing the searches the panel should jump to the first query.
findings.suggested_fix: Let synonym edits at step 3 save silently and only mark the searches out of date. If step 2 must reopen, show a confirm dialog first ('This will ask you to approve the topics again'). Auto-open the first Query after 'Write the searches'.

findings.what_happened: I only answered 4 questions, but the header says '5 of 5 questions', the panel says 'Scoping conversation: 5 questions', and the summary shows 'Which kinds of studies: not answered yet' and '5 of 6 answered'. The 'Where?' question was asked although 'Thailand' was already in my idea and shown as a topic. 'Keep 5 suggested topics' is followed by a second approval, 'Use these topics', which feels like asking twice. The topic 'Adult people' is odd and my 'blood sugar / HbA1c' answer did not become a topic.
findings.expected: Counts that match what I did. No question about something already known. One approval for topics.
findings.suggested_fix: Count asked and answered questions correctly. Skip a question when the field is already filled from the idea (offer 'Is Thailand right? Yes/Edit'). Merge 'Keep' and 'Use these topics' into one button, or explain the difference.

findings.what_happened: Many words are hard for a second-language reader: appraise/appraisal, synthesis, contested, synthesise, 'Query', 'Corpus', 'MeSH', 'PICO/PICo', 'title/abstract', 'left out of the synthesis', 'go forward', 'skim', 'fix any wrong cells', 'Markdown', 'BibTeX', 'Accept anyway'. I guessed 'Appraise selected papers' meant 'check the quality' and was unsure. I also read 'Found means the words are in the paper' only after re-reading.
findings.expected: Short plain words, or a small glossary on first use.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename: 'Appraise' to 'Check quality of papers'; 'Query' to 'Database search'; 'Corpus' to 'Papers found'; 'Synthesis' to 'What the papers say'. Add dotted-underline hover/tap definitions for MeSH, PICO, BibTeX, Markdown.

findings.what_happened: The checklist shows 'Keep 3-5 papers per topic, or every matching paper where fewer match' already ticked as Done, while the amber warning directly below says 3 topics have fewer than 3 matching papers (Diabetes patient only 1). Grammar in the warning is also 'only 1 matches'. The page opened scrolled down on arrival, so I missed the heading and checklist at first.
findings.expected: A task that is not really satisfied should not be ticked. Page should open at the top.
findings.suggested_fix: Tick the item only when every topic has 3 or more papers, or when the user explicitly accepts. Reset the scroll to top on step change. Fix 'only 1 matches' to 'only 1 paper matches'.

findings.what_happened: Combining two filters (Cross-sectional AND Review article) gives 'Showing 0 of 119: cross-sectional; review article. 119 papers are hidden' with no hint that the filters are combined with AND or which one to remove. On the retrieval page the Study type bars still show 119-paper totals after I filtered by article type, while the key below the chart updated. 'Review article 17' next to 'Systematic / scoping review 2' (later 10) feels contradictory without explanation.
findings.expected: An empty result should explain itself and offer a fix. Counts on one page should react consistently to the filter.
findings.suggested_fix: Show 'No papers match both. Filters work together (AND). Remove one: [Cross-sectional x] [Review article x]'. Make the bars show the filtered count or label them 'all papers'. Add one line explaining article type (journal's label) versus study type (design).

findings.what_happened: The landing page says it 'finds real papers in PubMed and OpenAlex' and shows a smooth example, with no mention that this server is a demo with scripted AI and unrelated recorded papers. The demo note appears only after sign-up, as a small dismissible bar with 8-pt text. On the account menu the same state is called 'Mock mode', not 'Demo mode'. After 'Start my review', the next page is titled 'Check your idea, then start' and asks me to start again.
findings.expected: Say once, before sign-up, that this is a demo. Use one name for the mode. One 'start' for the idea.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a one-line 'Demo version: sample papers only' chip under the landing CTA when demo mode is on. Use 'Demo mode' everywhere. Change step 1 headline to 'Check your idea' with the button 'Ask me questions'.

findings.what_happened: The 3D chart is cut off at the right edge of the panel on a 768 px tablet, and 'Height has no meaning yet' is odd. Zero-count study types (Cohort, Cross-sectional, Qualitative) stay in the key with a dimmed state, and one of them looked brighter than the others, so I could not tell what dimmed means. The default colour is study type, but 'Colour by' and 'Show as 2D chart' appear only after much scrolling. Colour and shape legend itself is clear and consistent with the table later.
findings.expected: A chart that fits the width and a legend where a dimmed item has an explained meaning.
findings.suggested_fix: Constrain the chart to the panel width. Add 'greyed = none in this set' to the key. Default to the 2D chart at widths under 900 px. Drop 'Height has no meaning yet' or say 'height is only for spacing'.

findings.what_happened: The report title and the project name are my raw idea with typos ('diabtes pateint ... there sugar level'), and the chosen question starts with '(mock)'. reports.categories_and_colours:
Found and understood without help. Study type has colour plus a shape plus a text label, and the same pairing is used everywhere I looked: blue circle for Trial, orange square for Cohort / case-control, green triangle for Cross-sectional, amber diamond for Qualitative / mixed methods, pink star for Systematic / scoping review, green cross for Other design, grey ring for Not reported. The shapes in the retrieval chart legend matched the shapes next to each paper in the summary table. Topics also get colour plus shape in the topic map, with a legend saying 'Each topic keeps this colour and shape in every view'.

Filtering by study type: chips in the table, with counts and a check mark when selected. This worked, and the page said 'Showing 13 of 119: cross-sectional. 106 papers are hidden by your filters (still in the review)' with a visible Reset filters. Filtering by article type (Journal article 86, Review article 17, Preprint 6, Editorial / letter / comment 10) also worked on both retrieval and the table. Article-type bars are plain grey, so colour never means two things.

Problems: (1) two filters from different groups are combined with AND, which gave 'Showing 0 of 119' with no explanation. (2) After an article-type filter on retrieval, the Study type bars still showed all-paper totals while the chart key changed. (3) Dimmed zero-count categories were not explained, and one looked brighter than the others. (4) Article type (journal label) versus study type (design) is never explained in one sentence, and 'Review article 17' versus 'Systematic / scoping review 2' looked contradictory. (5) The study-type counts changed a lot between step 4 (database labels, 102 not reported) and step 5 (AI reading, 17 not reported) without a note on the chips. (6) The 3D chart was cut off at tablet width. Totals did add up: 86+17+6+10 = 119 and 6+2+9+102 = 119, 90+125 = 215 fetched, and 215 - 96 duplicates = 119.
reports.validity_assessment:
The workflow is traceable and mostly honest about its limits, but in this demo it cannot yet prove it makes a valid review. Strengths: the demo banner and '(mock)' labels are clear. Every paper has real identifiers (DOI, PMID, PMCID, OpenAlex ID) and the abstract as returned by the database. Counts reconcile (215 fetched, 96 duplicates, 119 unique). Each synthesis statement links to quote chips that open the exact quote with 'Open paper', and the checker visibly flags a deliberately altered quote ('Blended mobile health which clearly proves the intervention works everywhere') as 'not found, you decide' with Accept anyway / Reject. 'Undecided' quotes are left out and the report counts them ('found 122; not found 12; accepted 0, rejected 1, undecided 11'). The report says it is 'a scoping aid, not an exhaustive systematic search' with a single reviewer. The novelty check says 'Finding no similar study does not prove a question is new' and, in demo mode, 'say nothing about whether your question is new'. No 'novel' claim was made. Warnings fire when topics have too few matching papers (Diabetes patient had only 1) and require 'Appraise anyway'.

Weaknesses: (1) The green 'found word for word' tick sits on quotes that are not relevant to the checklist question, and statements such as 'Known' are about review methods, so the green looks like validation of content. A reader with limited English may read it as 'verified'. (2) AI labels can be wrong without a visible warning (a narrative review labelled cross-sectional, a protocol's background shown as a key finding). (3) Selected papers were off-topic (precision medicine, e-mental health, HIV) and the pipeline still went on to a 'gap' and three candidate questions; the only guard was the per-topic warning and my confirmation. (4) Match counts like 'PubMed 7,629' are recorded numbers, labelled as samples only on the query page. (5) The chosen question keeps '(mock)' and the report title keeps my typos. Nothing looked fabricated: invented content is labelled '(mock)' and references come with identifiers. I could not judge real-mode quality in this run.
