reports.narrative:
I opened Athena on a tablet and understood the landing page quickly: type an idea, get a research question with real papers. I signed up and typed my sentence with its mistakes. The app did not fix them, but its 'What we know so far' box quietly turned 'diabtes pateint' into 'Diabetes patient', which I liked. The four short questions were easy, though it asked 'Where?' after I had already written Thailand, and it later said '5 of 5 questions' when I had answered four.

Step 3 confused me. I did not know MeSH, I added synonyms, and the app sent me back to step 2 to approve topics again. That felt like a wrong turn. After that the searches, the 119-paper count and the colour-and-shape legend all made sense. Filtering by study type and article type worked, but two filters together gave 'Showing 0 of 119' with no help.

The appraisal step was the hardest. Many green 'found word for word' ticks sat next to quotes that did not answer the question, and I only understood the warning after re-reading it. I liked that one altered quote was flagged 'not found, you decide', and that the app let me reject it. The synthesis was about review methods and telemedicine, not diabetes, but the demo banner and '(mock)' labels told me why, so I did not feel cheated. The three research questions were clear, and 'Finish and export' stayed locked until I chose one. The report was honest: it listed found, rejected and undecided quotes and said it is not a systematic search. It still used my typos as its title, and 'Markdown' meant little to me. I reached the report and the CSV preview, with no console errors.

findings.what_happened: The scoping chat ended after four answers (who, where, outcome, years). Focus jumped to the heading 'Turn your answers into search topics', so my fifth answer (study designs) was typed into nothing and Enter did nothing. No message said the answer was not saved. The summary still says 'Which kinds of studies: not answered yet' while the counter says '5 of 5 questions' and '5 of 6 answered'. 'South Asia' from my 'where' answer never became a search topic, only 'Sub-Saharan Africa'.
findings.expected: Either ask the fifth question or say plainly that the chat is over. Focus should land somewhere that accepts typing, or typed text should never vanish silently. Counts should agree with what is shown, and every place in my answer should appear in the topics (or the app should say which ones were left out).
findings.suggested_fix: When the last question is answered, announce 'Questions finished' and move focus to a clearly named next control. Keep the typed text if focus is not in a field. Make the counter reflect answered questions only, and list dropped places or terms with an option to add them.

findings.what_happened: After 'Write the searches' the open panel still said 'Viewing step 2 of 9 · Scoping · Edit this search topic' with the topic-name fields, but its primary button read 'Run all 10 searches'. I could not see the searches that had been written. Only after pressing Escape did the canvas offer 'Open step 3: Check the searches before they run'. I almost ran 10 searches I had never seen.
findings.expected: The panel should switch to the written searches (the plain-language concept blocks I saw later), or offer 'Go to step 3', as docs/ux-intent.md says a non-current panel should. The button should match the heading.
findings.suggested_fix: After 'Write the searches' succeeds, navigate the panel to the query node and move focus to its heading. Never show a step-3 primary action on a step-2 panel.

findings.what_happened: At 200% zoom the step panel fills the whole window, and the sticky title block plus the sticky footer leave a reading window of roughly 150 to 350 px. The focused answer box in the scoping chat is half hidden behind the footer. The 'Start my review' button is cut off at the bottom on the first page. Opening 'How this works' expands content that is out of sight below the fold, so nothing shows that anything happened.
findings.expected: A focused control should never be covered by sticky bars (WCAG 2.4.11). Expanded content should scroll into view. A fixed footer should not eat a third of a zoomed screen.
findings.suggested_fix: Add scroll-padding equal to the sticky footer and header height, call scrollIntoView on the focused element and on newly expanded sections, and make the footer non-sticky or compact when the viewport height is under about 500 CSS px.

findings.what_happened: After keyboard actions, focus is moved inconsistently. Pressing Reject on a quote sent focus to the panel heading at the top of a long paper, so I lost my place and had to Tab through about 30 stops to find the next quote (4 left to decide). Choosing candidate 1 also sent focus to the heading. Pressing 'Rank the papers' left the page scrolled to the bottom of the list with focus on 'Appraise selected papers', not on the new step's heading. Home and PageDown did nothing right after that.
findings.expected: After a decision, focus stays on, or moves to the next undecided item and the change is announced. After a step changes, focus and scroll go to the new heading.
findings.suggested_fix: Move focus to the next 'Accept anyway/Reject' pair (or to the 'Decided' status of the same card) after a decision. Reset scroll to top and focus the h2 on every step change. Add an aria-live message for each decision.

findings.what_happened: The checklist says 'Decide every quote the check could not find (0 decided, 5 left)', but the quotes I saw first in the quality checklist all carry a green 'found word for word'. The five undecided quotes are far down under 'Key findings'. Pressing 'Summarise the evidence' warns '5 quotes not decided yet', and I could not tell where they were. Tab order also puts 'Next paper' before the paper content, and the filter checkbox has no name.
findings.expected: The checklist item should link me straight to the first undecided quote. 'Show only quotes I need to decide' should be easy to find and clearly named.
findings.suggested_fix: Make '5 left' a button that jumps to and focuses the first undecided quote. Label the checkbox. Put 'Next paper' after the paper in DOM order.

findings.page: Sign up, step 3 topic fields, step 7
findings.what_happened: The focus helper reports an empty accessible name for the topic-name and synonym inputs and for the 'Show only quotes I need to decide' checkbox. The idea textarea is named by its placeholder, not by its visible label 'Your research idea'. On sign-up focus started on Email, not Your name.
findings.expected: Every field has a programmatic label that matches the visible one.
findings.suggested_fix: Associate each visible label with its input (for/id or aria-labelledby). Do not rely on placeholders.

findings.what_happened: The panel is not modal. From the panel heading, Shift+Tab goes to the hidden canvas controls (Zoom out, Fit view, Minimap) behind it, and Tab past the last button leaves the panel for the page behind. The panel hides those controls visually, so I was sometimes tabbing through controls I could not see. By contrast, the confirm dialogs (fewer than 3 papers, undecided quotes) trap focus and restore it on Escape correctly.
findings.expected: A panel that covers the screen should contain focus (or the page behind should be inert), like the dialogs do.
findings.suggested_fix: Set inert or aria-hidden on the canvas and header while a full-width panel is open.

findings.what_happened: The 3D scatter of papers cannot be reached or read by keyboard. Its dots have no tab stops. The legend buttons filter it well and a status line says 'Showing 5 of 94 papers', but I cannot find out which papers the dots are. Unselected legend entries are dimmed grey on dark, which is low contrast at 200% zoom.
findings.expected: Every paper in the chart can be reached by keyboard or the chart has a text alternative (the table in step 5 partly serves this).
findings.suggested_fix: Link to the paper table from the chart caption ('See these papers as a list') and raise the contrast of dimmed legend entries.

findings.what_happened: Within the paper details drawer, PageDown from the Close button did not scroll the drawer, so I could not read the abstract section by keyboard except by tabbing through its links. The drawer overlay leaves the table rows behind it in the Tab order. Focus did return correctly to the row on Escape.
findings.expected: The drawer body scrolls with the keyboard, and the rows behind are not reachable while it is open.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the scrollable region tabindex 0 and an accessible name, and set the table inert while the drawer is open.

findings.what_happened: The 9-segment strip is only coloured bars: green for done, white for current, dark for later. At 200% zoom I see no numbers, ticks or labels, so I rely on colour alone. docs/ux-intent.md says the strip should be numbered with done shown as a tick and never colour alone.
findings.expected: Numbers or ticks on the segments (and for 'out of date').
findings.suggested_fix: Add step numbers and a check icon in each segment, with an accessible name like 'Step 3, done'.

findings.what_happened: All 94 papers are about telemedicine in Southeast Asia, none about postpartum depression. The app is honest about this in many places (the banner, the step 3 notice, the step 6 'matches no topic', the step 8 'This review can say nothing about them', the novelty-check disclaimer). But the headlines still say 'Check which papers go forward', and the chosen question text begins '(mock)', which would be carried into the report. The '(mock)' tag is jargon, and the green 'found word for word' badge stays next to '(mock)' quotes. The banner can be dismissed with one key press.
findings.expected: A demo-mode user is never left thinking the sample papers are real results. A '(mock)' prefix should not become part of the chosen question.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep a small permanent 'Demo data' chip in the header after the banner is dismissed, replace '(mock)' with 'Example:' in the UI, and strip it from the editable question.

findings.what_happened: A quote can be 'found word for word' while the AI's answer is 'Unclear' and the quote is just the paper's title, so a green tick sits beside weak evidence. The caveat 'Found means the words are in the paper, not that they prove the answer' is only in a collapsed note.
findings.expected: The green tick should not look like approval of the answer.
findings.suggested_fix: Word the badge 'quote is in the paper' and show the caveat inline under the first quote.

findings.what_happened: After 'Start my review' I land on a project page that only repeats my idea and offers 'Open step 1'. Opening it shows 'Check your idea, then start' with another button 'Sharpen my idea'. That is two extra stops for the same sentence I just typed. 'What happens in this step' shows '8 s' with no explanation, and 'Hide this note' has no stated subject.
findings.expected: One typed idea leads straight to the first question.
findings.suggested_fix: Start the scoping chat directly after step 1. Label the timer 'Video, 8 seconds'.

findings.what_happened: Jargon without explanation: '0 MeSH' on every topic card, 'Controlled vocabulary (MeSH)' with the value 'none', PICo and PECO on candidate questions. A synonym 'whether peer-led groups' (mock) is nonsense.
findings.expected: A social-work lecturer should understand each term. MeSH should be explained once where it is first used.
findings.suggested_fix: Use an inline 'What is MeSH?' help text on first use, and write 'no official keywords found' instead of 'none'.

findings.what_happened: I pressed 'Download the report (Markdown)' and nothing on screen confirmed it. The three format cards are radio buttons whose descriptions mix grey and white text. 'Larger preview' only navigates to the same panel content on a new page. A label reads 'Found in openalex' in lowercase.
findings.expected: A visible confirmation such as 'Report downloaded' that is also announced to a screen reader. Consistent label casing.
findings.suggested_fix: Show an aria-live toast after download. Capitalise source names (OpenAlex, PubMed).

three_second_test.note: A guided literature review that turns a rough idea into a research question with real papers. I would press 'Start a review', then sign up. Focus ring is clear, and the skip link works.
Create an account. First I would type my email, then a password, then press Create account. The password rule is clear. Focus started on Email, skipping the optional name.
Describe my idea in a sentence. I would type it, then press 'Start my review'. At 200% the Start button is partly cut off and three example chips sit in the Tab order before it.
The page shows the project at step 1 with one big button 'Open step 1'. It repeats the idea I just typed, which felt like an extra stop.
Check my saved idea then press 'Sharpen my idea'. The panel covers the screen at 200%, and the focus moved to the heading, which is good.
Answer short questions in my own words and press Enter. Easy, but the answer box is half hidden by the footer and a '(mock)' prefix in the question is jargon.
Keep or delete suggested topics, then press 'Keep 5 suggested topics', then 'Use these topics'. The keyboard flow worked, but 'South Asia' was missing.
The panel said 'Edit this search topic / Viewing step 2' but offered 'Run all 10 searches'. I did not know what the searches were. I only found them by closing the panel.
Read the PubMed and OpenAlex searches in plain words, then press 'Run all 10 searches'. The demo-mode notice here is clear and honest.
See how many papers were found and how many duplicates, then press 'Summarise the papers'. The counts and the legend are clear, and every filter button works by keyboard.
Skim the papers and fix wrong cells, then press 'Rank the papers'. The to-do list helps. Rows are buttons, so I can open a paper by keyboard.
Check which papers go forward, then press 'Appraise selected papers'. The dialog warning '4 topics have fewer than 3 papers' is very clear, and focus is trapped correctly.
I could not tell which quotes needed my decision: the counter said 5 left but everything I saw was green 'found'. The undecided ones were far down the page.
Read what is known, contested and unknown, then press 'Suggest research questions'. The notice 'This review can say nothing about them' is excellent.
Compare three candidates and press 'Choose this question', then 'Finish and export'. 'Finish and export' is locked until I choose, with a reason shown.
The review is ready: check the question, pick Report, CSV or BibTeX, and press Download. The preview begins with 'Demo: ... not a real review'. After downloading nothing confirmed it.

reports.categories_and_colours: Study type has a colour and a shape for each category. The legend and counts match in the retrieval step, the table filter chips and the 3D chart: Trial is a blue circle, Cohort/case-control an orange square, Cross-sectional a green triangle, Qualitative/mixed methods an amber diamond, Systematic/scoping review a pink star, Other design a green cross, and Not reported a grey ring. I understood these without being told, because every shape sits next to a text label and a count, and the 'Colour by' menu says which dimension the colours show. Article type (Journal article 72, Review article 11, Preprint 4, Editorial/letter/comment 7) is plain grey, so colour never means two things on one screen. By keyboard I could find and filter papers by study type and by article type in step 4, step 5 and step 6. Pressing Enter on a chip showed an explicit message ('Showing 11 of 94: review article. 83 papers are hidden by your filters') and a 'Reset filters' button. Counts add up: study type 5+1+7+81 = 94 and article type 72+11+4+7 = 94. At step 4 the study-type bars show 81 'Not reported', but after AI summarising in step 5 only 13 are 'Not reported' and 39 'Other design', so the numbers change between steps (the page says so). Two different taxonomies can confuse: 'Review article' (11) versus 'Systematic / scoping review' (8) are different counts and one review-article paper is labelled 'Other design'. In the 3D chart, the dimmed legend entries are low contrast. The chart's dots cannot be reached by keyboard.
reports.validity_assessment: Within demo mode the workflow is mostly traceable and honest. Every paper has DOI, PMID and OpenAlex identifiers and an open-access status. AI-drafted cells are labelled 'AI · abstract'. The app deliberately plants an altered quote ('clearly proves the intervention works everywhere') to show the verification: it is flagged 'not found, you decide' with the closest passage and a 54% word match, and only accepted quotes are used. Undecided quotes are excluded from the synthesis, and the exported report states 'Quotes found: 47; not found: 5 (accepted by you 0, rejected by you 1, undecided 4)'. The app never overclaims novelty: 'Finding no similar study does not prove a question is new', and the demo novelty check says it says nothing about novelty. The step 6 and step 8 warnings say my topics have no evidence ('This review can say nothing about them'). Weak points: (1) all papers are about telemedicine in Southeast Asia, so the chosen question '(mock) How do mothers with postpartum depression experience peer support groups...' is not backed by any real paper on the topic, and the '(mock)' prefix ends up in the question and report. The mock supporting quote comes from a smart-home review. (2) The 'found word for word' green tick appears on quotes that do not support the AI's answer, such as the title quoted for 'Unclear'. (3) 'South Asia' vanished from the topics and the study-type answer was lost without notice, so the search does not reflect what I said. (4) The report says it is a scoping aid with a single reviewer and no second check, which is honest. I could not test real mode, so I cannot say whether a real run would produce valid questions.
reports.would_have_quit_at: I reached the exported report and would not have quit. The closest points were (1) Step 3, where the panel still showed 'Edit this search topic' next to a 'Run all 10 searches' button and I could not see the searches, and (2) Step 7, where I could not find the five quotes needing a decision and each Reject sent focus back to the top of a long page. A real keyboard user with a tremor would likely give up around the quote decisions (5 decisions each costing about 30 Tab presses) or accept 'Summarise without them', as I did.

reports.categories_and_colours: Found without help: yes. Step 4 shows "Article type (from the databases)" bars (Journal article 81, Review 11, Preprint 5, Editorial 9, Other 1) and a separate "Study type (only where the database labels it)" list. Step 5 and 6 have two rows of filter chips, "Study type" and "Article type", each with counts. Clicking chips filtered correctly ("Showing 15 of 107: cross-sectional; journal article. 92 papers are hidden by your filters (still in the review)" with a visible Reset filters), and the "Colour by" select, legend and 2D/3D toggle exist. I understood the encoding without being told: each study type has a colour plus a shape plus a text label (blue circle Trial, orange square Cohort, green triangle Cross-sectional, amber diamond Qualitative, pink star Systematic/scoping review, green plus Other design, grey ring Not reported). Article type chips are plain ink, which keeps colours from meaning two things. Counts reconcile: 4+2+8+93 = 107 and 81+11+5+9+1 = 107. Misleading or confusing points: (1) study-type counts change between step 4 (Trial 4, Not reported 93) and step 5 (Trial 6, Not reported 18) after the AI reads abstracts; step 4 explains this, but the numbers still jump. (2) Green (Other design cross, Cross-sectional triangle) and amber (Qualitative diamond) are also the app's "done/success" and "your turn/out of date/warning" colours on the same screens, which breaks the one-colour-one-meaning rule. (3) "Review article 11" (article type) versus "Systematic / scoping review 7" (study type) reads as two different counts of reviews until you read the headings. (4) The 3D point cloud says "Height has no meaning yet", has little axis labelling and clips points at the right edge; the 2D chart is better. (5) Empty categories are dimmed in the legend but still listed, which is a nice touch but easy to miss. Other "Colour by" options (topic, source, evidence status, score) were not tested.
reports.validity_assessment: Mostly grounded and unusually honest, with a few traps. Strengths: the demo banner is dismissible and clear (scripted AI, recorded telemedicine papers, "(mock)" text); it is repeated in the search panel, the table and the report header ("Demo: scripted AI and recorded sample papers; not a real review"). Every paper keeps an identifier and a real abstract that expands inline beside the AI row; each ranking has a "Why this score" breakdown with formulas; each quality-check answer carries a quote, and the quote is checked word for word. The demo deliberately altered quotes ("...which clearly proves the intervention works everywhere"), flagged them "not found, you decide", showed the closest real passage ("50% of words match") and left rejected or undecided quotes out of the synthesis. Synthesis chips open the exact quote with "found word for word", "Open paper" and "Pin to canvas", and the Contested statement tells the user to read both quotes before treating it as a real disagreement. Candidate novelty is not overstated: "Finding no similar study does not prove a question is new", and in demo mode "these are recorded sample records, so they say nothing about whether your question is new". The report says it is a scoping aid, not an exhaustive search, that one reviewer (you) selected the papers, and its numbers reconcile (15,309 summed hits, 135 collected, 107 unique, 76 quotes found, 7 not found with 1 accepted and 6 rejected). Warnings stop a user from drifting on: "Few papers match 2 topics" in step 6, the "2 topics have fewer than 3 papers" pop-up before appraising, and "No evidence for 2 topics... This review can say nothing about them" in step 8. Editing an approved step marks later steps out of date instead of silently rewriting them. Weaknesses: (a) the landing page promises "real papers... every quote checked" without saying this server is demo, so the demo is only disclosed after starting. (b) Counts conflict: Attention span shows PubMed 2,207 / OpenAlex 1,630 matches in step 4 but "0 of 0" papers in step 6. (c) A paper with "0 topic terms appear in title/abstract" still scores 58/100 and ranks #4. (d) Candidate 3 ("What helps or hinders short-form video apps among teenagers...") is a template sentence that does not make sense, and an edited question keeps the Gap, Feasibility and Weakness text written for the original. (e) A raw citation blob appears as a "key finding". Nothing looked invented, but a user who ignores the banners could believe a telemedicine review is about their topic; real-mode validity cannot be judged here.
reports.narrative: I landed on the home page and understood it in a few seconds: turn a rough idea into a research question using real papers. I signed up, and a weak password was rejected with a clear message. I typed my topic, double-clicked Start, and still got one project, which pleased me. The canvas map is pretty, though "Sharpen my idea" and "Open step 1" felt like twins. I answered one scoping question, reloaded (my draft vanished but my place stayed), skipped the rest, and mashed "Suggest search topics" with no harm done. Back dropped me on My projects and I resumed fine. I deleted the wrong topic by accident; Undo saved me, but it came back labelled "added by you". The first real hesitation was step 3: after "Write the searches" the panel still said "Edit this search topic / Viewing step 2", and clicking a search card on the canvas did nothing. I only found the actual searches by switching to List. Retrieval was quick, and the type bars, the legend and the filters made sense without help. Ranking and appraisal were dense but trustworthy: the score breakdown, and the fake quote shown beside the nearest real passage, impressed me. Appraisal panel space is tight; I had to hunt for the content. I chose a question, reworded it, and downloaded the report. Then I went back and changed step 6; the "Edit an earlier step?" dialog and the amber "3 out of date" markers were excellent. The foreign project URL just said it could not be opened, and logged out it asked me to log in. I never felt stuck, only occasionally unsure where the real content was.

findings.what_happened: After Write the searches, 8 Query cards appear and the header says step 3, but the side panel stays on 'Edit this search topic' with the label 'Viewing step 2 of 9 · Scoping'. Clicking a Query card on the canvas only highlights it; the panel does not open that search. The actual PubMed/OpenAlex search groups appeared only after I switched to List and clicked a Query row.
findings.expected: Clicking a Query card (or finishing Write the searches) opens 'Check the searches before they run' for that search, with the step label matching step 3, as the List view does.
findings.suggested_fix: After writing searches, auto-select the first Query node and show the search panel; make canvas card clicks update the panel the same way List rows do; show 'Step 3 of 9' in the panel header.

findings.what_happened: Step 4 shows Attention span 'Ran: PubMed 2,207 · OpenAlex 1,630' and Teenagers 'PubMed 2,207 · OpenAlex 412'. Step 6 then says Attention span '0 of 0' and Teenagers '0 of 40' with 'no papers match'. A user cannot tell whether thousands of papers exist for those topics or none.
findings.expected: Counts that agree, or a short sentence saying 'hits reported by the database' versus 'papers collected and matching this topic'.
findings.suggested_fix: Label the step 4 numbers 'database hits' and add 'collected for this topic' beside them; explain in step 6 why a topic with thousands of hits has 0 matches.

findings.what_happened: A paper explained as 'Topic fit 1/5: 0 topic terms appear in title/abstract' and labelled 'does not match the topic' still shows a score of 58 out of 100 and ranks #4, above papers marked 'weak match' that are selected. The headline number looks decent while the label (small grey text) says it is irrelevant.
findings.expected: A score that drops with no topic match, or a clear cap so irrelevant papers are not ranked above relevant ones.
findings.suggested_fix: Cap the total when topic fit is 0 or 1, or sort 'does not match' papers below matching ones, and make that label as prominent as the score.

findings.what_happened: Candidate 3, '(mock) What helps or hinders short-form video apps among teenagers aged 13 to 17 in secondary school?', is a template sentence that does not make sense for this topic, and its gap talks about 'barriers and enablers compared across settings'. After I reworded Candidate 1, the card was marked 'edited' but kept the original Gap, Feasibility, Weakness and Structure text.
findings.expected: Candidates that read as plausible questions for the user's idea, and edited questions that either refresh or clearly flag that the surrounding assessment was written for the original wording.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'assessment is for the original wording' under an edited question, or offer 'Re-check this question'; improve the wording template for exposure-type topics.

findings.what_happened: The landing page says 'It finds real papers in PubMed and OpenAlex... every quote checked against its source' and 'You get a report'. It never says this server is a demo returning recorded telemedicine papers; that is first disclosed on the project page. The account menu says 'Mock mode' while the banner says 'Demo mode'.
findings.expected: A demo server should say so on the first page, and use one term for it throughout.
findings.suggested_fix: Show a small 'Demo server: scripted AI, sample papers' line on the landing and sign-up pages when demo mode is on; rename 'Mock mode' to 'Demo mode'.

findings.page: Sign up, New review, Log in
findings.what_happened: 'Create account', 'Start my review' and 'Log in' look identical (bright blue, full strength) whether they are usable or not. Clicking 'Start my review' with an empty box does nothing at all and gives no message; my automated click timed out because the button was truly disabled. Only the small grey text 'Write at least a sentence to start' hints at the reason.
findings.expected: A visibly dimmed disabled state, or an enabled button that explains what is missing.
findings.suggested_fix: Give disabled buttons a clearly muted style and aria-disabled with the reason, or keep them enabled and show an inline message.

findings.what_happened: After deleting 'Short-form video apps' (an AI suggestion) and pressing Undo, the topic came back at the bottom labelled 'added by you', with no Edit, Keep or Delete controls, and stayed labelled that way through approval. Its provenance is wrong, and it cannot be changed in the same list view.
findings.expected: Undo restores the topic exactly as it was (in place, still 'suggested', with its controls).
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the original record and order on Undo; keep the 'suggested' origin.

findings.page: Step 7 appraisal and step 8 synthesis panels
findings.what_happened: At 1366x900 the sticky panel header, 3-item checklist and explanatory paragraph take about 60% of the panel height. In appraisal the first screen shows only the paper title and an 'Abstract only' badge; the quotes to decide are below the fold. In List view the page scrolls the left list, not the panel, so I only reached the content by switching to Canvas or tabbing in.
findings.expected: The paper's quality checklist and quotes visible on first view, or a compact checklist that collapses after the first visit.
findings.suggested_fix: Collapse the 'Do these things' box and the explainer paragraph to one line once seen, or let the main content scroll under a slimmer header.

findings.what_happened: Appraisal and Synthesis cards show a green '✓ 76' with no label. I only found out in the report that it means 76 quotes found word for word.
findings.expected: A label such as '76 quotes verified', or a tooltip.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the word 'quotes' or a tooltip to the badge.

findings.what_happened: While viewing a search (already step 3 of 9) the primary footer button reads 'Go to step 3: Search builder'. It really runs a different panel and the real action 'Run all 8 searches' only appears after clicking it.
findings.expected: The footer action should be 'Run all 8 searches' on this panel, per the page's own intent.
findings.suggested_fix: Make Run all N searches the primary action whenever step 3 is the current step.

findings.page: Step 4 map and legends, table, stepper
findings.what_happened: Colour meanings collide on one screen. Green marks 'Other design' (cross) and 'Cross-sectional' (triangle) in the legend while green also means done/approved in the stepper; amber marks 'Qualitative / mixed methods' while amber also means 'your turn', warnings and out of date. The 3D chart says 'Height has no meaning yet', gives only 2015 and 2026 as axis labels, and cuts off points at its right edge.
findings.expected: One colour, one meaning per screen, as the UX intent says; a chart whose every axis means something.
findings.suggested_fix: Move status colours (done, your turn, stale) to a hue outside the category palette, or never show both in one view; default to the 2D chart or drop the meaningless 3D axis.

findings.what_happened: The Study type and Article type filters I set in step 5 (Cross-sectional + Journal article) were still applied when I arrived at step 6, so the ranking showed 'Showing 15 of 107' and hid 92 papers until I clicked Reset filters. The page does warn about hidden papers.
findings.expected: A new step starts unfiltered, or says that the filters were carried over.
findings.suggested_fix: Reset filters when moving to another step, or show 'Filters from the last step are still on'.

findings.what_happened: The top-ranked paper's key finding is a raw citation blob ('(mock) Horst.Technology Literacy as a Barrier to Telehealth During COVID-19.Telemedicine and e-Health.Sep 2020.1118-1119.http://doi.org/...Published in Volume: 26 Issue 9...') rather than a finding. It sits in the most prominent row.
findings.expected: A short finding sentence, or 'No finding extracted from this abstract'.
findings.suggested_fix: Detect abstracts that are mostly citation metadata and show 'Not reported' instead of a finding.

findings.what_happened: Adding synonyms to an approved topic reopened step 2, marked the Idea as 'Your turn' again and forced me back through 'Use these topics'. The warning was shown before and after the change, and I could return correctly, but a small tweak costs two extra screens.
findings.expected: Either re-approval is only needed for changes to topic names, or synonym edits get a single 'Save and keep step 2 approved' choice.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat synonym changes as a lighter edit that invalidates only the searches, not the topics approval.

findings.what_happened: Pressing Back inside a project (even from a step three panels deep) leaves the project and returns to My projects, because moving between steps does not add history entries. State was preserved every time, but in-project Back does not go to the previous panel.
findings.expected: Back returns to the previous panel or step; leaving the project should take a deliberate action.
findings.suggested_fix: Push history entries when the selected node or step changes (the ?node= parameter is already in the URL).

findings.what_happened: The 'What we know so far' header shows 'questions done' with no number, and the canvas card still says '2 of 5 questions' after the rest were skipped.
findings.expected: '2 questions answered, rest skipped' or similar.
findings.suggested_fix: Render the count when questions are skipped and update the card text.

findings.what_happened: On the canvas the side panel covers the topic and query cards (Accept/Dismiss buttons are cut off); on the landing page the animated demo clips its left column ('d uptake'). An unsent scoping answer was lost on reload, and /admin silently redirects to My projects with no message.
findings.expected: Fit the canvas to the visible area when the panel opens; a short notice when a page is not available to the user.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-fit the canvas when the panel opens; save the answer draft locally; show 'You do not have access to that page' on redirect.

findings.what_happened: The dashboard contradicts itself for the chaos user. The top tile says Projects 2, '1 finished', and the funnel footer says '1 of 2 projects finished all nine steps'. The same funnel shows 6. Ranking = 1 (0 approved) and 7. Appraisal, 8. Synthesis and 9. Research question = 0. The Accounts row for leo.chaos@example.com says Furthest step '6 of 9'. Leo says he reached step 9, exported, then went back and deselected a paper, which marked 3 later steps out of date.
findings.expected: One consistent story. Either 'finished' and the funnel both count the high-water mark (Leo reached step 9 once), or both count current approved state, in which case 'finished' would be 0. A funnel titled 'projects that reached each step' should not drop to 0 for steps a user has already reached.
findings.suggested_fix: Decide whether the funnel and 'Furthest step' show the high-water mark or the current approved state. Use the same rule for 'finished', the funnel and the account table. If you keep current state, label it 'currently approved' and show 'out of date' as its own count so a user who went back is visible as such.

findings.what_happened: I could not reconcile the clinician's account with the dashboard for the appraisal step. The clinician says 9 papers were selected and 10 quotes were decided. The dashboard shows 8 appraisal calls (appraisal v1 = 8). Comparable servers matched one call per paper: 4102 had 8 papers and 8 calls, 4103 had 11 and 11, 4105 had 13 and 13, 4106 had 5 and 5. The dashboard has no per-project paper counts, so I cannot say whether this is an honest difference (for example one paper reappraised or skipped) or a miscount.
findings.expected: An admin can tell why 9 selected papers produced 8 appraisal calls, or sees a note such as 'papers without full text are not sent to the model'.
findings.suggested_fix: Show a small per-account detail: papers collected, selected and appraised, and calls per step. Or add a one-line explanation of how calls map to papers.

findings.what_happened: The tile titled 'Latency p50 / p90' shows a dash, and its subtext reads 'p90 - / p99 -'. The title and subtext name different percentiles, and the dash is not explained. In demo mode there is no latency, but the page does not say so.
findings.expected: Matching percentile labels, and 'No live calls in demo mode' (or similar) instead of a bare dash.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the title and subtext use the same percentiles, and replace the dashes with a short reason.

findings.page: /admin top tiles: 'Server errors (1 h)' on all servers
findings.what_happened: The request denominators look implausibly small next to what users did: 4101 shows '0 of 2 requests', 4102 shows 1, 4103 shows 245, 4104 shows 809. Uptime on every server is about 35 min, while accounts say 'Joined 1 hour ago'. The counters seem to cover only the time since the process started, but the tile says '1 h'. A '0% errors' reading backed by 2 requests could mislead an admin.
findings.expected: Either the counter survives restarts, or the tile says 'since restart (35 min)' and shows a 'not enough data' state when the count is very low.
findings.suggested_fix: Label the window honestly ('since server start'). Show 'too few requests to judge' below a threshold.

findings.what_happened: The audit log masks emails (for example 'email: m...@example.com') but prints the full address right beside it ('signup by mai.undergrad.qa3@example.com'). The masking has no effect. The Accounts table also lists full emails. That is reasonable for an admin, and no research ideas, titles, papers, notes, keys or emails in URLs appeared anywhere on any dashboard. The privacy promise on counts and metadata holds, but the masking is inconsistent.
findings.expected: One consistent rule: either show full emails everywhere in the admin area and drop the masked copy, or mask them in the audit log.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the duplicate masked email, or mask the actor name in the audit log.

findings.page: User view during AI pause (http://localhost:4102/s/prj_91e8b5644ca94c47, step 2 Scoping)
findings.what_happened: The pause is handled well, with a plain banner on every page. 'Sharpen my idea' still looks active, and clicking it fires a request that returns HTTP 503. A reload fires another, so one user action counted 2 'blocked, not sent'. The scoping panel shows an empty header band above a disabled textarea reading 'Waiting for the next question...'. The step-1 canvas card still says '0 of 5 questions' with nothing explaining that the questions are waiting on the pause.
findings.expected: The AI-dependent button is visibly disabled, or says 'AI is paused' on the button itself. No empty box. The blocked counter counts decisions, not retries.
findings.suggested_fix: Disable the AI buttons while the pause is on, with a tooltip or label. Hide the empty textarea header. Do not auto-retry on reload, or do not count retries as separate blocked calls.

findings.what_happened: The funnel bars change from light to dark blue as the step number rises, with no legend. In a chart that otherwise uses colour for meaning, a reader will wonder whether the shades mean something. The 'Where people stop' list is all zeros on every server, so it carries no information when nobody is stuck.
findings.expected: One colour for one meaning, per the app's own rule, or a legend or note if the shade means something.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a single colour for the funnel. Collapse the 'Where people stop' list into one sentence when every count is 0.

findings.page: http://localhost:4102/login?next=/admin and an ordinary user opening /admin
findings.what_happened: An admin going to /admin and sent to login sees the heading 'Log in to continue your review'. An ordinary user opening /admin while logged in is silently redirected to My projects with no explanation.
findings.expected: The admin login says what it is for ('Log in to open the admin dashboard'). A non-admin sees a short 'This page is for administrators' message.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a next-aware login heading, and a notice when a non-admin is redirected away from /admin.

findings.page: /admin AI & API key panel after turning AI off
findings.what_happened: The 'Turn AI back on' button sits almost touching the 'Models' row below it (a few pixels of gap) when the Off state adds a 'Changed just now by...' line. The warm warning colour and the text are fine, but the layout feels cramped.
findings.expected: Normal spacing between the primary action and the next row.
findings.suggested_fix: Add bottom margin to the status column or the panel so the button is not flush with the Models row.

findings.what_happened: The dashboard has no way to confirm that users exported. The step-9 'approved' count is the closest thing. Users reported previewing the report, downloading Markdown, and switching to CSV or BibTeX, and none of that is visible. The admin cannot tell whether the last step produced a deliverable.
findings.expected: Possibly a count of reports exported, if that is meant to be a health signal. If not, the page could say so.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an 'exported' count to the funnel, or state that exports are not tracked.

three_second_test.note: A guided literature review tool. I would click Log in first, then enter the admin account. The headline and the two buttons are clear.

three_second_test.note: 'Is Athena healthy?' with a green 'Everything is healthy' banner is readable at once. I would read the AI & API key panel next, then the tiles. It found the admin dashboard under Account and settings > Admin dashboard, which was easy to find. On 4107 the amber/green state was equally clear.
'Turn AI off for everyone?' says what will and will not stop (no calls, no spend, work kept, searches keep working). The red 'Turn AI off' button is distinct from 'Keep AI on'.
An amber 'Needs your attention: AI is switched off' banner, 'Off' status with who changed it and when, and a bright 'Turn AI back on' button. Very clear.

three_second_test.page: User canvas/step panel while AI is paused
three_second_test.note: The amber 'AI is paused by the administrator. Your work is saved.' banner is plain and reassuring. A user would understand it. The canvas around it is busy and the 'Sharpen my idea' button still looks live.

admin.categories_and_colours: I did not reach paper lists, maps or charts of study types or article types: as admin I only looked at the dashboard, and the ordinary user I created stayed at scoping. I could not check study-type or article-type filtering or the legend. On the dashboard, the charts use one blue hue. Funnel bars shade from light to dark blue by step with no legend, so a reader could wonder whether the shade carries meaning (minor/polish finding). Status colours are consistent and readable: green = healthy, amber = needs attention or AI paused (banner and the Off state). The red 'Turn AI off' button reads as a destructive action. Colour is never the only signal, because each state also carries an icon and a text label.
admin.validity_assessment: Dashboard counts match what users reported on six of the seven servers, and the AI on/off control is honest. 4101 (Mai): 2 users incl. admin, 1 project finished, funnel 1 at all 9 steps, 59 AI calls ('scoping' 6 calls for 5 questions + topics). 4102 (Daniel): 46 calls, appraisal 8 for 8 papers. 4103 (Aisha): 54 calls, appraisal 11 for 11 papers. 4105 (Somchai): 60 calls, summaries 13 matches '13 of 13 batches', appraisal 13 for 13 papers. 4106 (Ruth): 39 calls, summaries 11 matches '11 of 11 batches', appraisal 5 for 5 papers. 4107: double-submitting buttons did not double-count calls (1 topic_importance, 1 scoping_topics, 1 research_questions call), and 1 failed login matches Leo's wrong password. The two issues are the 4107 contradiction ('1 finished' vs funnel steps 7 to 9 at 0 vs account '6 of 9') and the unreconciled 9-papers-to-8-appraisals on 4104. Privacy: across all 7 dashboards, charts and tables, I saw only counts, step names, prompt names, account emails and timestamps. No research ideas, project titles, papers, notes or keys. URLs carried only project ids. Full emails appear in the Accounts table and next to masked ones in the audit log, so masking is cosmetic. The AI kill switch test on 4102 passed: with AI off the user saw 'AI is paused by the administrator. Your work is saved.' on every page and in the step panel, the step did not proceed and no mock text was invented, the AI call count stayed at 46 and the dashboard showed '1 blocked, not sent' (then 2 after a reload), spend stayed $0.00, and the Search state was fine. After turning AI on, the user's scoping resumed without any action (first question appeared) and answering worked; calls rose from 46 to 48, which fits 1 auto-resumed start + 1 answer. I did not touch any key (status 'No key', demo mode) or the spend limit. The demo-mode banner is honest that sample papers are on telemedicine in Southeast Asia and that AI text is marked '(mock)'. I did not check traceability of statements to quotes, or 'novel' wording, because I never reached steps 7 to 9 as a user.
admin.would_have_quit_at: I would not have quit. The only point of real doubt was the 4107 dashboard, where the funnel and the account row said Leo was at step 6 while the tile said '1 finished'. An admin would stop trusting the funnel there until it was explained.
admin.activity: About 75 helper commands in two browsers (admin and admin-check-user). Admin logged in on all 7 servers with the shared admin account. Per server (dashboard vs user account): 4101 Mai: Users 2 (1 admin), Projects 1 finished, funnel 1 at all 9 steps, 59 AI calls, 0% failed, 0 errors, $0.00; MATCH. 4102 Daniel: Users 2, 1 project finished, funnel 9 of 9, 46 AI calls (appraisal 8), 0 errors; MATCH. 4103 Aisha: Users 2, 1 project finished, 54 AI calls (appraisal 11), 0 errors; MATCH. 4104 Okafor: Users 2, 1 project finished, 41 AI calls (appraisal 8 vs 9 selected papers, summaries 7); MOSTLY MATCH with one unreconciled count. 4105 Somchai: Users 2, 1 project finished, 60 AI calls (summaries 13, appraisal 13), 0 errors; MATCH. 4106 Ruth: Users 2, 1 project finished, 39 AI calls (summaries 11, appraisal 5), 0 errors; MATCH. 4107 Leo and someone.else: Users 3, Projects 2 with '1 finished', 42 AI calls, 1 failed login (matches Leo's wrong password), 0 server errors; MISMATCH between 'finished', the funnel (steps 7 to 9 at 0) and Leo's account ('6 of 9'), likely caused by the stale-after-edit state. someone.else shows 1 of 9 with 0 AI calls, correct. AI kill switch on 4102: turned AI off through Turn AI off... and confirmed. Created user admin-check-user@example.com and project prj_91e8b5644ca94c47. Pressed 'Sharpen my idea' while AI was off (HTTP 503 on scoping/start, expected), reloaded (second blocked). Call count stayed 46, showing '1 blocked, not sent' and then 2. Turned AI back on; the user's scoping resumed by itself, I answered question 1 and got question 2; calls rose to 48. No console errors on any admin page. Never touched the key or the spend limit. Cookies are shared across localhost ports, so logging into another server logged the admin browser out of the previous one; that is an environment effect, not an app finding.
admin.narrative: I started from scratch because no earlier screenshots existed. I opened server 4101, logged in as admin and looked for the dashboard the way an admin would: Account and settings then Admin dashboard. That was easy to find. The top of the dashboard answered 'Is Athena healthy?' with a green banner within a couple of seconds, and the AI & API key panel came next, as the page intends. I compared each server with what its user said. Six of the seven matched closely, and the AI-call breakdown by step even reproduced numbers like 13 of 13 summary batches and 5 appraisals for 5 papers. That gave me real confidence in the counters. The one place I stopped and frowned was 4107, the chaos server. The tile said '1 finished', but the funnel showed nothing at steps 7 to 9 and Leo's account row said '6 of 9'. Leo had gone back and made later steps stale, so the numbers are probably each correct under different rules, but together they read as a contradiction. I also noticed the request counters were tiny on a few servers, and the latency tile had mismatched labels. For the AI test I turned AI off on 4102 and the confirmation dialog was excellent. As a new user in the second browser I got a calm, honest 'AI is paused by the administrator. Your work is saved.' message, nothing was faked, and the dashboard showed '1 blocked, not sent' while the call count stayed at 46. After I turned AI back on, the user's scoping resumed by itself. I never saw a key, an idea or a paper on any dashboard.
